articles.title: John Cena Reveals His Match Routine, WWE Rumors on Seth Rollins' Injury, Roman Reigns & LA Knight
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Cena Discusses How He Prepared for Matches

Nearly one year after competing in the final match of his illustrious career, WWE legend John Cena provided some insight this week into how he prepared for matches during his nearly 25 years in the company.

During an appearance Thursday on What Now? With Trevor Noah (beginning at the 46:20 mark of the podcast) , Cena provided some insight into his routine prior to matches:

Cena noted that early in his career, he would just do "a couple of jumps," before "running out there like a Tasmanian devil," once his music hit.

However, Cena explained that his process became much more involved as he got older and more experience in the wrestling business.

Cena referenced a "flexibility protocol" that began two hours before his matches, adding, "I'd have to maintain a certain warmth and heart rate an hour in to make sure you're always moving around and always stretching. I'd have to practice more, like the difficult things I knew I could do in my sleep, especially the strength-based stuff that I was known for. Because I could probably do that, but I'm not as strong as I used to be."

On top of that, Cena stressed the importance of recovery after his matches, including icing himself down.

Cena's final match took place last December against Gunther at Saturday Night's Main Event, ending one of the most successful careers in pro wrestling history.

A record 17-time world champion, Cena reached the top and remained there for much of his career, which speaks to his longevity.

Everything Cena did before and after his matches contributed to his lengthy run, and allowed him to step away from pro wrestling with his health largely intact.

Rollins Reportedly Dealing with Minor Injury

There is reportedly a bit more to Seth Rollins' absence from WWE programming than simply waiting for the right creative.

According to Dave Meltzer of the Wrestling Observer Newsletter (h/t WrestlePurists ), Rollins is dealing with a "minor" injury, and WWE is giving him some time to heal up.

However, if WWE needed him in the fold right now, Rollins would reportedly be healthy enough to return now or in the near future.

Meltzer added that WWE wants to bring him back for "maximum impact," and is waiting for the right time for that to be the case.

Rollins was last seen on WWE programming at SummerSlam in early August when he lost a World Heavyweight Championship match against Roman Reigns in the main event.

Although he did return to the ring in September, it was only for a handful of six-man tag team matches during WWE's live event tour of South America.

None of the matches aired on TV, meaning Rollins has now been absent from WWE programming for over two months.

Rollins is not slated to compete this weekend at Money in the Bank, but one can only assume WWE would like to have him reintegrated in time for Survivor Series next month.

Given the show of respect he and Reigns had following their match at SummerSlam, perhaps an alliance between them in a WarGames match against 946 is possible.

The World Heavyweight Championship match between Roman Reigns and LA Knight is reportedly expected to be in a featured spot Saturday night at Money in the Bank.

According to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t H Jenkins of Ringside News), the plan is for Reigns vs. Knight to headline Money in the Bank as the main event.

That doesn't come as a big surprise since Reigns' matches go on last more often than not, while Knight is a hugely popular babyface challenger in his own right.

Given their history, Reigns vs. Knight has been a highly anticipated clash, and the excitement continued to grow Monday thanks to a strong promo segment on Raw.

Per WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t Felix Upton of Ringside News), there was "considerable acclaim" for the segment from people within WWE.

Multiple WWE officials were reportedly "particularly impressed" with the emotion Reigns showed, noting that there were "genuine discussions about how effective that version of Reigns could be moving forward in the appropriate setting."

The OTC has turned in strong performance after strong performance since beating CM Punk for the world heavyweight title at WrestleMania 42, and he has been more active in terms of appearances and matches since then than he had been for multiple years prior.

Reigns is firing on all cylinders, but Knight has a ton of support in his own right, which should make for a highly entertaining MITB main event with a fun atmosphere.

articles.title: WWE SmackDown Winners, Live Grades, Reaction and Highlights Before Money in the Bank 2026
articles.summary: Before we get to the Money in the Bank PLE on Saturday, WWE had one last stop to make in Lafayette, Louisiana for this week's SmackDown.
articles.body:
Before we get to the Money in the Bank PLE on Saturday, WWE had one last stop to make in Lafayette, Louisiana for this week's SmackDown.

All of the competitors for both MITB matches were in attendance to hype the show and make their arguments for why they will win the briefcase.

While the main focus was on the PLE, we did get a women's tag title match this week with Charlotte Flair and Tatum Paxley challenging Lainey Reid and Fallon Henley.

Let's take a look at everything that went down on this week's show.

The show began with Adam Pearce and Nick Aldis talking about Money in the Bank. Trick Williams and Bron Breakker both showed up, and it led to them being booked in a singles match for later in the show.

Back in the arena, CM Punk made his way to the ring to kick things off. He talked about why he would compete in a dangerous match like MITB at this stage in his career. He climbed up the ladder and said he has a chance to make history as the only three-time MITB winner, so he is willing to take the risk.

He talked about each competitor, which led to Kevin Owens joining him in the ring. They traded some personal insults as KO climbed up the second ladder in the ring. Sami Zayn was the next one to come out, and he had a big smile on his face.

This was a pretty cut-and-dry segment. It didn't really add anything to the MITB match, but it gave the three guys in the ring a chance to win the crowd over. It probably went on longer than it needed to, but it wasn't bad. It just wasn't great either.

When they all of the MITB competitors walking around, Lola Vice looked at her fist, as if she wanted to make sure it was still there.

Lil Yachty isn't necessary for Williams to get over, but sometimes he can be kind of funny. His exchange with Breakker backstage was good.

Punk and Owens are funny together. Their exchange when Sami Zayn came out was hilarious.

Roxanne Perez, Lola Vice and Sol Ruca vs. Lash Legend, Tiffany Stratton and Jacy Jayne

All six women who will compete in the MITB match took part in a six-woman tag match. The teams were mixed in an unusual way, so both sides had heels and babyfaces, which seemed like an odd choice since there were three of each.

Roxanne Perez was looking to outshine her partners and tagged herself in early in the match, but as soon as Lash Legend came in, she tried to get out of the ring. Lola Vice and Sol Ruca dropped off the apron to avoid a tag and made her deal with Legend herself.

All of these competitors have talent and bring something different to the ring, but some matches just don't end up having the necessary chemistry, and this was one of them.

There were multiple awkward moments that seemed like someone missed a timing cue, or it simply didn't make sense, like when Stratton completely ignored Ruca so she could climb up and hit a moonsault, which was then followed by the same move from Ruca.

The match had its moments, so it wasn't all bad, but this definitely felt more like a series of sequences thrown together than a cohesive match with a story that flowed from start to finish.

Legend scored the win for her team by pinning Ruca with her finisher. As soon as it was over, Legend took out Jayne and Tiffy to show that she was serious about winning MITB.

There were some issues playing Ruca's entrance music.

Vice and Legend had a weird start to their sequence, but Vice being so aggressive with her strikes made it fun.

Ruca completely missed her moonsault to Legend, but she sold it anyway.

Jayne was the standout in this match. She didn't hit the most exciting moves, but she showed the most charisma.

Ruca rarely wears the same style of gear twice in a row. It must make it hard for the figure and game designers to decide on a look for her.

Charlotte Flair was attacked by Jade Cargill, Michin and B-Fab backstage before the break. When the show returned, she was trying to tell Aldis she would be fine to compete, but medical wouldn't clear her. Flair told Alexa Bliss to take her spot.

Back in the arena, Tama and Talla Tonga came out with Haku to take on The War Raiders, Erik and Ivar. Erik and Talla started for their teams, and the Tongan immediately knocked the Viking down with a clothesline.

This was a pretty physical match with a steady pace, but it didn't feel like things picked up until after the break. Shinsuke Nakamura and Kyoki showed up to distract the tag champs, and it helped give the War Raiders the upper hand.

When it looked like Erik and Ivar might win, Haku interfered and used his walking stick to hit Erik in the throat. Tama and Talla hit their tag team finisher to get the win. Bakusai immediately attacked the champions when it was over.

The War Raiders losing a non-title match won't do them any favors, but at least the tag titles are still being kept in the spotlight.

Nikki Bella had a segment with Chelsea Green backstage. She needs a new angle on her character because the same old mean girl act she has been doing is worn out.

It felt like the mid-match break came earlier than usual.

It was nice to hear the announcers put over the careers all four men had in Japan before WWE.

Cody Rhodes Will Never Be Rid of Randy Orton

During a backstage segment, Aldis informed Danhausen that he would be facing Gunther tonight, which did not sit well with the painted man. We also saw Aldis tell Randy Orton he could have the night off and sent him home.

Out in the arena, The Miz and Kit Wilson showed up to demand respect, but they were interrupted by Cody Rhodes. The American Nightmare took out both men, and then Aldis came out and said this is exactly what he was trying to avoid when he sent Orton home.

The GM said Cody and Randy fighting anywhere other than in the ring doesn't help anyone, so he proposed Rhodes come to his office to talk about their options. Rhodes said no and that he needs this match booked. Then the segment ended without it being booked.

This might not have been an original segment, but Rhodes did a decent job carrying it. The Miz and Wilson are great stooges who are willing to do whatever it takes to make someone else look good.

Danhausen had an evil detector backstage and it seemed to think Finn Balor was evil.

In one of the oddest matchups we have seen in quite some time, Gunther took on Danhausen this week.

Before Danhausen could curse The Ring General, he kicked the painted man in the face and started decimating him. The match never officially got started, so the ref tried and failed to get him to relent.

Balor showed up to give Danhausen some assistance. He took down Gunther a few times and forced him to escape through the crowd, but he came back while Balor was checking on Danhausen and attacked him from behind.

There was no actual match, but Gunther destroying Danhausen and Balor was definitely entertaining. He needed to look dangerous again, and this segment did that while also setting up Balor vs. Gunther for the future.

Damian Priest attacked Fraxiom backstage after they told him to apologize to R-Truth. After he was done, Truth showed up and started brawling with him.

Zayn had a backstage segment with Johnny Gargano and Candice LeRae.

Fatal Influence vs. Tatum Paxley and Alexa Bliss (Women's Tag Titles)

After Charlotte was taken out earlier in the night, Bliss replaced her to team with Paxley in a tag title match against Reid and Henley.

Bliss started in the ring and had a brief moment of being in control before the champions double-teamed her. Tatum tagged in and gained the upper hand momentarily, but the champions sent her crashing to the floor as the show went to a break.

This match had people at every experience level. Reid was the newest with just three years since she began training; Paxley has only five years; Henley has been wrestling for almost nine years; and Bliss is going on 13 since joining WWE.

That difference in experience was extremely evident in the ring, but all four women did a decent job. The thing that caught a lot of people off guard was Bliss and Paxley scoring the win to become the new tag team champions.

Result: Bliss and Paxley won the tag titles

The purple gear was a nice change of pace for Paxley.

The finisher Paxley uses is hit or miss, but the one she hit at the end looked great.

This week's main event was booked at the top of the show. Breakker took on Williams before both men compete in the MITB match this weekend.

The match got started with less than 10 minutes left in the show, so we knew this was not going to be a battle of attrition. Breakker took control right out of the gate and hit a clothesline from the apron to send Williams over the announce table.

There was no stakes to this match, but WWE wanted you to believe that whoever won would gain momentum heading into the PLE.

They kept a good pace and made the action feel physical and hard-hitting, but they simply didn't have enough time to put together the kind of match that would stand out much.

Williams and Breakker are both probably going to be world champions someday, so this could be a preview of a PLE main event a few years from now. They seemed to work well together, and they will almost certainly gain more chemistry in the coming years.

Sadly, the match ended in a disqualification when The Vision showed up and attacked Williams. Evans came out to help Williams, which didn't make much sense since they weren't allies in any way.

The show ended with Bronson Reed hitting Williams with a Tsunami.

Breakker told Zayn he would see him soon during a backstage segment, so it looks like we know which belt he will chase if he wins.

Breakker's entrance might need to come with a possible seizure warning.

When the main event is only getting the last nine minutes of the show, putting a break in the middle of it feels cheap.

Friday's SmackDown may have done its job of hyping the Money in the Bank event on Saturday, but most of what we got this week is skippable.

The only match you should probably see is the women's tag title bout since the belts changed hands, but even that didn't stand out much.

With the level of talent WWE has on the roster, it's disappointing to see a show only register as mediocre at best.

Tomorrow's PLE has the potential to be great, especially if certain people win their matches, but the go-home SmackDown was nothing to write home about.

articles.body:
Portland Trail Blazers guard Damian Lillard ranked seven of the best professional wrestlers of all time (all of whom saw action in WWE) during a segment that aired on social media Friday.

Here's how the nine-time All-Star broke them down.

S Tier (Elite): The Rock, Ric Flair, The Undertaker

A Tier: Shawn Michaels, Triple H, Bret Hart

Lillard clearly loves Stone Cold Steve Austin, based on his comments.

"I'm gonna start with the GOAT, because that's the easiest one for me, Stone Cold Steve Austin," Lillard said.

Lillard also shouted out Stone Cold on X after the Blazers released the video.

That love has been known for some time. Lillard once showed up to a Blazers home game in Oct. 2018 with a Stone Cold mask, an iconic Austin 3:16 T-shirt and a championship belt.

The 36-year-old Lillard grew up during the Attitude Era, which obviously made a great impact on him. It's clear that respect for the legends (particularly Stone Cold) lives on to this day.

articles.title: Igor Shesterkin Injured, Latest News on Rangers Star's Status After Exiting vs. Capitals
articles.summary: New York Rangers star goaltender Igor Shesterkin was helped off the ice Friday after suffering an apparent leg injury in the second period of a game against the Washington Capitals.
articles.body:
New York Rangers star goaltender Igor Shesterkin was helped off the ice Friday after suffering an apparent leg injury in the second period of a game against the Washington Capitals.

Shesterkin fell to the ice after attempting a save by lunging into a split with his right skate blade braced against the goalpost.

Dylan Garand took over for the Rangers in net following Shesterkin's exit from the game, which was tied at 1-1 with 11:40 remaining in the second period.

Shesterkin was putting no weight on his right leg as he was helped off the ice by two teammates.

Losing Shesterkin would be a major blow for the Rangers, which began the season 4-1-0 in part thanks to the netminder's strong start.

The former Vezina Trophy winner had posted a .926 save percentage while allowing just 1.75 goals against per game through his first four starts of the season.

He also scored the first goal of his NHL career to cap off the Rangers' home-opening win against the Tampa Bay Lightning.

The Rangers are already missing No. 2 goaltender Joonas Korpisalo, who was placed on injured reserve with a lower-body injury after the season opener. Garand was recalled from the AHL in a corresponding move.

Rangers coach Mike Sullivan said Korpisalo had not resumed skating as of Thursday, per Mollie Walker of the New York Post.

AHL goaltender Spencer Martin, who would normally be fourth on the Rangers' depth chart behind Garand, is also day-to-day with a lower-body injury.

That could lead to the Rangers turning to Callum Tung, who started for the AHL's Hartford Wolf Pack Friday night in Martin's absence, as a backup for Garand should Shesterkin miss any time.

That would leave the Rangers with an inexperienced goaltending tandem. Tung has yet to make his Rangers debut, while Friday night's substitution marked Garand's fifth appearance at the NHL level.

The Rangers will hope to hear good news regarding Shesterkin before Sunday's matchup against the visiting Vancouver Canucks.

articles.title: How Neeraj Chopra's javelin helped Rohit Yadav win Asian Games bronze
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: When Rohit Yadav stepped onto the field in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, for the Asian Games javelin final, he carried more than a piece of sporting
articles.body: NEW DELHI: When Rohit Yadav stepped onto the field in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, for the Asian Games javelin final, he carried more than a piece of sporting equipment. In his hand was a signed javelin belonging to Olympic and world champion Neeraj Chopra — a quiet gesture of support that would accompany him to an international podium.The story began in June, when Yadav struck gold at the National Inter State Senior Athletics Championships in Bhubaneswar with a personal best of 87.05m. Upon returning to his training base in NIS Patiala, he discovered that his preferred javelin had bent, apparently during air transit in its protective PVC tube in the aircraft’s cargo hold.Yadav subsequently competed at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow with a borrowed implement, finishing seventh with 81.56m in cold, windy conditions. With the Asian Games approaching, he faced the prospect of competing without his trusted javelin.“For the Asian Games, I didn’t have my own javelin. My preferred one was damaged and had bent. While coming to Delhi from Patiala for the Indian Athletics Final Series on Sept 10, I spoke to Neeraj bhai,” Yadav told TOI.“We have been in regular touch. I knew he had returned to India for rehabilitation. I told him I didn’t have a javelin of my own for the Asian Games. He immediately came to my rescue and sent me one of his signed javelins through a private taxi service to the Jawaharlal Nehru (JLN) stadium,” he added.Chopra had withdrawn from the remainder of the season, including the Asian Games, to recover from an ankle ligament injury. His absence left India without its two-time defending champion, but his gesture ensured that a fellow Indian thrower had the equipment he needed.There was, however, a catch. Yadav could not use the javelin in Delhi because it had not been registered with the Technical Information Centre (TIC) for inspection. He borrowed another registered implement for the event, then carefully packed Chopra’s gift for Japan.“At the Asian Games, I registered two javelins with the TIC. But I used the one Neeraj bhai gave me. I had a good grip and hold over it, and with that javelin I made the winning throw to secure bronze with 84.35m,” he said.“I will remain thankful to Neeraj bhai. I have kept that javelin with me and will use it in future competitions as well.”After his competition, Rohit listened to Chopra’s congratulatory voice message.“He told me to enjoy the win and savour my first big international medal. He said that when he returns fully fit, we will compete together, and that I have a long way to go.”Back home in Uttar Pradesh’s Jaunpur, Yadav is taking the off-season to spend time with family until Diwali.“I want to earn a Diamond League entry, compete internationally and qualify for the World Championships next year. The ultimate target remains the Los Angeles Olympics,” he added.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 5 key numbers from Iowa football's 41-24 win over Washington
articles.summary: The Hawkeyes won 41-24 at Washington on Friday. Here are five key numbers that tell the story of the game.
articles.body:
The Iowa football team had a successful trip out west, beating Washington 41-24 on Oct. 9.

Jeremy Hecklinski made his first career start under center and threw for three touchdowns. Kamari Moulton scored two touchdowns of his own and hit a career-high with 208 rushing yards.

Here are five numbers that tell the story of the Hawkeyes' win over Washington.

One of the biggest questions surrounding Iowa's offense was why wasn't the run game succeeding? On Friday night, the Hawkeyes cracked the code.

Moulton rushed for a career-high 208 yards on 26 carries. His previous best was 183 in the first game of the season against Northern Illinois.

He scored two touchdowns, one on a 56-yard rush where he found the gap, broke a handful of tackles and juked a defender to get the first touchdown of the game.

Moulton scored his second of the day in the fourth quarter, on a 3-yard rush.

Moulton's 208 yards were the most for an Iowa player in a road game since Marcus Coker had 252 at Minnesota in 2011, Big Ten Network reported.

Hecklinski made the most of his first collegiate start.

After an impressive showing during the Kids Day at Kinnick preseasaon scrimmage, Hecklinski fell short in the battle for Iowa's starting QB job. Hank Brown had started the first five games of the season before injuring his shoulder against Ohio State last week.

Brown was listed as a "game-time decision" on Friday's pregame availability report and did not appear in the game. Hecklinski, meanwhile, put on a show. He finished with 14 completions on 19 attempts, good for 202 yards and three touchdowns — two to DJ Vonnahme and one to Reece Vander Zee.

The Hawkeye defense sacked Washington quarterbacks a total of six times; five in the first half. The Huskies lost 50 yards on those six plays.

Cam Buffington and Preston Ries had two apiece and Jayden Montgomery and Bryce Hawthorne each recorded one.

Iowa was leading 27-3 heading into halftime and added on from there. This was Iowa's highest-scoring conference road game since tallying 51 at Maryland in 2021, according to Big Ten Network.

1965: The last time Iowa won in the regular season in the Pacific time zone

The last time the Hawkeyes were successful in a Pacific time zone regular-season game was a 27-7 win over Oregon State. It was Iowa's only win all season.

articles.title: Bouchard's Crazy Start And What Oilers Fans Can Make Of It
articles.summary: Through four games, Evan Bouchard has six goals and 11 points, and yet, there are still people who would rather talk about what he does wrong.
articles.body:
Through four games, Evan Bouchard has six goals and 11 points, and yet, there are still people who would rather talk about what he does wrong.

Edmonton Oilers fans are very good at finding something to criticize about No. 2, and don't get me wrong, sometimes he gives them a lot to work with, but he's also coming off a 95-point season, led every NHL defenceman in scoring last year and has started this season putting up numbers that haven't been seen in more than a century.

At some point, maybe we can forgive him for the occasional defensive mistake.

Bouchard scored twice and added an assist in Wednesday's 5-2 win over the Anaheim Ducks, bringing his season total to six goals and 11 points. He's leading the entire NHL in goals, sitting behind only Connor McDavid in points, and has already scored nearly a third of the 21 goals he managed over 82 games last season.

The last defenceman to score six goals through his first four games was Harry Cameron, who had eight with the Toronto Arenas in 1917-18. Bouchard is also the fifth defenceman in NHL history to record at least 10 points through four games, joining a group that includes Bobby Orr, Pat Stapleton and Morgan Rielly.

There aren't many opportunities to mention Bouchard and Orr in the same statistical conversation, although Bouchard seems determined to create a few.

His teammates have been talking about him with a certain amount of admiration for quite some time, and Leon Draisaitl had an interesting response when asked about how Bouchard is perceived around the league.

"It's pretty funny how he's viewed around the league, in my eyes. But people can continue to see it that way, and we'll gladly have him on the ice," Draisaitl said.

Draisaitl understands everything that comes with Bouchard's game, including the mistakes that often end up on our social media feeds the next day. That said, he's also one of the players who benefits from having a defenceman who contributes offensively and creates scoring opportunities at a level most teams simply don't have on their blue line.

Edmonton has outscored its opponents 11-1 at five-on-five, making it hard to argue that his presence is hurting the Oilers when they're producing results like that.

Bouchard has also been carrying considerable responsibility on Edmonton's blue line, playing over 25 minutes a night and helping to drive an offence that has already scored 19 goals over four games.

His production last season was enough to consider him for the Norris Trophy. However, the Norris goes to the best overall defenceman, and at the time, his scoring did not make up for his defensive lapses. he eventually finished fourth in voting behind Zach Werenski, Cale Makar, and Quinn Hughes, and he admitted last May that being left off the final ballot bothered him.

"When I saw that come out, I was definitely upset a little bit," Bouchard said on TSN OverDrive. "Stings a little bit, but you know what? You get back at it, and you forget about it."

Four games into the following season, he's leading all three of those defencemen in scoring, and there's already some discussion about whether this could finally be the year he receives serious consideration for the award.

Bouchard hasn't said that's what's driving his start, although it wouldn't be particularly surprising if finishing fourth after leading every defenceman in scoring left him with something to prove.

The Norris Trophy is a tough one for Bouchard because of the way his defensive game is perceived. Makar, Hughes, and Werenski have established themselves among the league's best, and Bouchard is trying to convince voters that his offensive production deserves the same recognition.

Let's be clear though, if Bouchard were to conitnue at his current pace, he would score more than 200 points—that's a bit much, even for Oilers fans. Let's also be clear, at some point he'll mess up and somebody watching said game will be wondering why Edmonton is paying him $10.5 million per season, it's just part of his game.

However, the people who play alongside him don't seem nearly as concerned about those mistakes as everyone watching from home. Draisaitl's comments are a pretty good example of how highly he's regarded in Edmonton's dressing room, where his teammates see the opportunities he creates throughout an entire game.

Oilers fans can keep complaining about No. 2 whenever he makes a mistake in his own end, but for now, though, maybe enjoy what he's doing with the puck. There aren't many defencemen in the NHL capable of it, and Edmonton happens to have one of them.

Ashton Taylor's three touchdowns propelled Westlake (7-2) to a commanding 43-6 victory over Cedar Valley (1-8) in their Region 2 matchup. Taylor's scoring began with a 3-yard pass from Silas Taumoepeau at 6:22 in the first quarter. Cedar Valley found their only points with a 1-yard run by McCrae Miles in the second quarter. Westlake extended their lead further with Slone Sua's 95-yard interception return and Taylor's 1-yard run in the third quarter. Spencer Dickerson and a 32-yard pass from Taumoepeau to Sua sealed the win in the fourth quarter for the Thunder.

Max Stevens secured the victory for Herriman (7-2) with a 16-yard touchdown run early in the fourth quarter, lifting the Mustangs to a 23-20 win over Region 2 rival Copper Hills (6-3). Copper Hills led 13-7 at halftime, thanks to Ishmael Duffus' 65-yard touchdown catch and two field goals by Lincoln Anderson. However, Herriman rallied in the second and third quarters to take the lead. Ethan Hill's 20-yard touchdown run brought Copper Hills within three points late in the game, but the Grizzlies couldn't complete the comeback.

Mountain Ridge Sentinels (9-0) overwhelmed the Bingham Miners (3-6) in a dominant 52-7 victory in a Region 2 matchup. Jaxon Hunt starred for Mountain Ridge, throwing four touchdown passes, including a 51-yard strike to Xander Thayer with 3:45 left in the first quarter for a 10-0 lead. Thayer caught three touchdowns in total, contributing significantly to the Sentinels' first-half 38-7 advantage. Tyson Dunn added two rushing touchdowns, with a notable 51-yard run at 6:14 of the second quarter. Bingham's lone score came from a 6-yard pass to Charlie Olson late in the second quarter.

Hunter's Wolverines (3-6) secured a decisive 24-8 victory over Cyprus (2-7) in a Region 4 matchup. Akuila Gallegos kick-started the scoring with a 14-yard run in the first quarter and later added a 43-yard touchdown run to give Hunter the lead for good, scoring with 11:17 left in the second quarter. Cyprus's only response came swiftly in the first quarter on a 31-yard pass from Izaiah Fabela to Rushton Langford. Hunter extended their lead in the second half with a 22-yard field goal by Ashton Arpero and Ryder Paea's 3-yard rushing touchdown in the fourth quarter.

In a dominant defensive display, West (9-0) shut out Granger (4-5) with a 52-0 victory in their Region 4 matchup. The Panthers set the tone early with three first-quarter touchdowns, starting with an 18-yard run by Derendrick Dixon with 9:50 left in the first. Takeshi Savery followed with a fumble recovery for a touchdown just over a minute later at 8:07. Kamden Lopati added a 6-yard rushing score at 2:25. Naeata Hamilton's 9-yard run expanded the lead to 30-0 at 4:37 in the second. West scored in each quarter, maintaining control throughout the game.

Juab (7-2) secured a 31-24 victory over Cedar City (4-5) in a 3A South game with a late surge. With 4:52 left in the fourth quarter, Juab's Price Armstrong connected with Will Armstrong on a critical 13-yard touchdown pass, putting the Wasps ahead for good. Cedar City responded quickly, as Beckett Wood returned a kickoff 97 yards for a touchdown with 4:37 remaining, narrowing the gap. However, Juab's defense held firm to secure the win. Notable contributions included Juab's Quentin Robinson's 7-yard touchdown in the first quarter and Brady Gempeler's impressive 44-yard reception just before the fourth quarter.

Ben Taulapapa scored four touchdowns for the Templars as Manti (2-7) defeated Carbon (1-8) 41-16 in a 3A South game. Taulapapa's performance included a pair of touchdown runs and a 24-yard touchdown reception, with all three scores coming in the first half to help Manti secure a commanding 28-10 lead at halftime. Kingston Wright contributed to Manti's dominance with two touchdown passes, including an early 11-yard pass to Kooper Lund with 9:49 left in the first quarter. Carbon's Kayden Dunn connected with Tayger Timothy and Brodee Collins for Carbon's lone touchdown passes.

Trey Yardley led Richfield (7-2) past Canyon View (6-3) in a 3A South showdown, scoring three touchdowns, including a 41-yard run with 8:10 left in the fourth quarter. Richfield pulled away early, taking a 17-3 lead into halftime following Ngalu Taufatofua's 2-yard touchdown run and Sam Gonzolez's 36-yard field goal. The Wildcats extended their advantage in the third quarter with Yardley's 25-yard touchdown run and Taufatofua's 1-yard touchdown reception. Canyon View's Preston Higgins caught a 4-yard touchdown pass with 3:12 left, but the Falcons' rally fell short, finishing with a 38-16 loss.

Ian Mair's dual threat performance led South Summit (5-4) to a commanding 36-12 victory over Judge Memorial (1-7) in a 2A North game. Mair opened scoring with a 3-yard run with 6:24 left in the first quarter and later connected on two touchdown passes, including a 44-yard strike to Cash Rockhill and a 22-yard pass to Brody Larsen. South Summit's defense held Judge Memorial scoreless in the first half and limited them to just 12 points overall. Brody Larsen also contributed with a 22-yard touchdown catch in the fourth quarter.

Beckham Meredith's standout performance propelled Summit Academy (6-3) to a dominant 51-6 victory over Providence Hall (2-7) in a 2A North game. Meredith caught two touchdown passes, including a 57-yarder from Rigby Young with 8:35 left in the third quarter that helped extend the Bears' lead. Summit Academy jumped out to an early lead, scoring 22 points in the first quarter alone and maintaining control throughout the game. Providence Hall's lone score came on a 90-yard kick return by Gary Grayson with 10 seconds left in the third quarter. Summit Academy's defense held strong, preventing any offensive points from the Patriots.

Beau Yeomans led San Juan (who 8-1) to a decisive 55-7 victory over Emery (2-7) in a 2A South matchup. Yeomans threw five touchdown passes, including a 25-yarder to Quincy Singer and a 26-yarder to Randall Black in the first quarter, followed by a 41-yard strike to Andrew Nielson as time expired in the same quarter. Brigg Palmer added rushing touchdowns of 90 and 50 yards. Miken Keith's 90-yard kick return in the third quarter sealed the blowout. Emery's sole score came from Ajay Thomas with a 5-yard run in the third quarter.

Tayton Pace led North Summit (6-3) to a come-from-behind victory against Millard (4-5) by connecting on two fourth-quarter touchdown passes in their 1A North matchup. The first was a 29-yard strike to Zach Ernst with 7:38 remaining, bringing the Braves within striking distance. Then, with 1:30 left in the game, Pace found Cru Richins for an 18-yard score, followed by a successful pass to Zach Ernst for the two-point conversion, securing the 17-14 win. Millard had taken a 14-3 lead earlier, with a second-quarter touchdown pass and a third-quarter rushing score.

Mccoy Coates ran for three touchdowns as the Gunnison Valley Bulldogs (5-4) crushed the North Sevier Wolves (2-7) 48-0 in a 1A North game. Coates opened the scoring with a 40-yard run at 7:31 of the first quarter and added a 6-yard touchdown run early in the second quarter. Gunnison Valley's defense blanked North Sevier, contributing to a decisive shutout. Axton Sorensen passed for two touchdowns, including a 40-yarder to Ryder Donaldson, helping the Bulldogs secure a 27-0 halftime lead. Chance Hammond's 48-yard run extended the lead in the fourth quarter, as the Bulldogs dominated throughout.

Jake Christensen's impressive performance propelled the Enterprise Wolves (5-4) to a commanding 48-0 victory over the Parowan Rams (1-8) in a 1A South game. Christensen scored three touchdowns, including a standout 61-yard run with 3:57 left in the second quarter, contributing significantly to Enterprise's dominance. The Wolves raced out to a 21-0 lead in the first quarter and maintained their momentum with another 21 points in the second quarter. Additional touchdowns by Rigz Anzalone, Aiden Ennen, Brannoc Davidson, and Easton Hill rounded off the scoring. Parowan failed to score as Enterprise's defense held firm throughout the game.

Dixie (2-7) dominated from the start with a commanding 47-0 victory over Cottonwood (0-9) in a nonregion matchup. Riker Muhlestein threw three touchdown passes, including a 35-yarder to Gus Morby and a 12-yarder to Robbie Bennett. Kingston Harwood's 3-yard run and Johnny Jessop's 67-yard punt return helped the Flyers jump to a 21-0 lead in the first quarter. Brygunn Soderquist's 17-yard interception return in the second quarter widened the gap. The Flyers' defense stifled Cottonwood (record unknown), holding them scoreless throughout the game.

McCrae Wade led Delta (7-2) to a decisive victory over American Leadership (5-4) with an early 17-yard touchdown run just 3 minutes and 33 seconds into the game. Delta dominated the first half, leading 42-0 at halftime after scoring six unanswered touchdowns, including a 58-yard pass from Davis Covey to Jacen Johnson. American Leadership's only score came in the third quarter with a 7-yard run from Mason Ober. Austin Jacobson sealed the win with a 1-yard run in the fourth quarter, bringing the final score to 49-7 in this nonregion matchup.

Davis Carter sparked Beaver (5-4) to a 27-7 nonregion win over North Sanpete (6-3) with his impressive all-around performance, including a 74-yard touchdown pass to Emmet Lurth early in the second quarter and a late 28-yard scoring run with 7:42 left in the fourth quarter. Beaver led 14-7 at halftime and sealed the victory with Leonardo De Leon's 33-yard touchdown run with 4:27 remaining. Beaver's defense shut out North Sanpete in the second half, holding them scoreless despite Luke Lee's first-half 1-yard touchdown run for the Hawks.

Faith Lutheran edged Desert Hills (3-6) 23-20 in a thrilling nonregion matchup. The Crusaders took an early lead with 3 points in the first quarter and expanded their advantage in the second, leading 13-7 at halftime. Desert Hills rallied in the third quarter with a 17-yard touchdown pass from Deacon Virgin to Seth Brown, cutting the deficit to 13-14. However, Faith Lutheran secured the win with a late go-ahead score of 10 points in the fourth quarter, holding off Desert Hills' late attempt, which included a 3-yard touchdown run by Tieg Andersen with 3:01 left.

Kyson Despain powered Duchesne (8-1) to a decisive 28-0 victory over Kanab (7-2) in a nonregion matchup, scoring all four of the Eagles' touchdowns. Despain opened the scoring with a 3-yard run with 8:41 left in the first quarter and added a 2-yard run in the second quarter to give Duchesne a 14-0 halftime lead. He continued his dominant performance with a 7-yard touchdown run late in the third quarter and sealed the win with an 8-yard score with 3:17 left in the fourth quarter. Duchesne's defense shut out the Cowboys, allowing zero points throughout the game.

Trapper Farnsworth's second-quarter interception return for a touchdown put South Sevier (3-5) ahead for good, leading to a 55-27 nonregion victory over Rich (6-3). With the score briefly tied at 14, Farnsworth's 25-yard return sparked a 21-point quarter for the Rams, including scores by Masen Healey and Cooper Castle. Farnsworth also contributed offensively with a 10-yard touchdown run in the third quarter. South Sevier maintained their lead despite a 37-yard touchdown run by Rich's Brady Cornia early in the third. Quarterback Rayce Freeman connected twice with Daxton Lovell for touchdowns, solidifying the Rams' decisive win.

In a defensive struggle, Grand (6-2) emerged victorious over Panguitch (3-5) with a final score of 15-9 in their 1A 8-player matchup. Both teams were held scoreless in the first quarter, showcasing strong defensive efforts on both sides.

Water Canyon (6-3) edged past Utah Military Camp Williams (4-5) with a defensive 12-7 victory in a 1A 8-player game. The Wildcats secured the win with a critical score late in the contest, as they held the Marauders to just seven points throughout the matchup.

Braxton Hansen's standout performance propelled Milford (5-4) to a decisive 51-6 victory over Utah Military Hillfield (3-5) in 1A 8-player action. Hansen accounted for three touchdowns in the first half alone, beginning with a 60-yard run late in the first quarter to extend the Tigers' lead. He then caught a 22-yard pass from Tyce Barnes early in the second quarter and added a 10-yard rushing score later. Tyce Barnes notably returned an interception 65 yards for a touchdown in the third quarter. Utah Military Hillfield managed only a single touchdown in the second quarter.

articles.title: Ex-Maple Leafs Forward Reveals What Phil Kessel Was Really Like as a Teammate
articles.summary: Former Maple Leafs forward Viktor Stalberg reflected on his time with Phil Kessel in Toronto, revealing what made Kessel a great teammate. The post Ex-Maple...
articles.body:
Former Maple Leafs forward Viktor Stalberg reflected on his time with Phil Kessel in Toronto. Stalberg revealed that Kessel was a great teammate and somebody he enjoyed being around.

Toronto selected Stalberg 161st overall by the 2006 NHL Draft.

Stalberg joined the Maple Leafs during the 2009-10 season after three strong seasons with the University of Vermont. There, he played with Kessel, who was also in his first season with Toronto after being acquired from the Boston Bruins.

Viktor Stalberg Reveals What Phil Kessel Was Really Like as a Teammate on the Maple Leafs

Viktor Stalberg only played with Phil Kessel for one season on the Maple Leafs.

Despite only spending only a brief period as Kessel's teammate, Stalberg looks back fondly at his time with the Leafs. He noted that the American was a big character in the locker room and someone he spent a lot of time with.

"[Kessel was a] funny guy, awesome guy. I spent a lot of time with him in Toronto. We were both fairly young at the time, me and Phil, and Tyler Bozak hung out a lot when we were up there," Stalberg exclusively told Heavy Sports via Ozoon . "He's a character, I like the guy. He loves his fast food, his hot dogs, and looks more like a mailman or something in terms of athleticism. I don't know if he's ever lifted a weight but he's just a naturally gritty, strong guy."

Stalberg added: "He was just so naturally gifted, so naturally strong, and, you know, the career he had was incredible. Offensively, he did everything."

Stalberg Shares Thoughts on Kessel Breaking the NHL Iron Man Record

Stalberg also shared his thoughts on Kessel setting the NHL 's new iron man record. The three-time Stanley Cup champion holds the record for the most consecutive regular season games played.

He revealed that Kessel was much stronger than he looked and would occasionally make a point of proving that.

"Phil Kessel breaking the NHL Iron Man record? That is something I would not have bet a single dollar on, after playing with him," Stalberg exclusively told Heavy Sports via Ozoon. "I think the strength coach in Toronto was chirping him for not doing anything in the gym, so he'd go in wearing flip-flops and squat more than anybody else on the team."

"He was so fast and honestly, in such poor shape in terms of hockey. And I know one year Toronto forced him to go on a diet, and lose some body fat pretty much to try and take it to the next level, and he was dog [expletive]."

Stalberg also pointed to Kessel as being an anomaly because he thrived without prioritizing dieting and fitness.

"There is not one formula that works for all, and whatever worked for him, worked for him. He was one of the best players in the league," Stalberg said. "He maybe didn't go in for the most battles in the corners, you can say that, but he was still such a gritty, tough guy."

articles.title: Tommy White's Contact Skills Stood Out in Debut Season with A's
articles.summary: Tommy White was called into action a little before he was deemed ready, but he showed plenty of promise in his time with the Athletics.
articles.body:
When injuries began to pile up for the Athletics in July, they called upon corner infielder Tommy White to get an opportunity with the big-league team. The 23-year-old may not have been ready for his debut, but the A's roster needed him, so he was thrust into action.

Across 56 games with the A's in the second half of the season, White ended up batting .254 with a .272 OBP and a wRC+ of 57 (100 is league average). He was able to collect hits at a nice clip, but just eight of his 48 hits on the year went for extra bases. For a corner infielder, the expectation is that as he continues his development, those numbers will tick up.

"Just trying to be an everyday guy," White said of what he's looking to work on going into the offseason. "Playing with that fire every single day. Staying on top of things in the training room. Things I've never really done in my career."

When young players come up to the big leagues for the first time, there is a lot of talk about them finding their own process or routine and settling into that before they feel comfortable. White said it took him maybe a month or two to find his, but now he has a set plan.

White's biggest moment of the season (apart from perhaps his MLB debut) was the game he had back home against the Tampa Bay Rays on September 16. He ended up going 3-for-4 with a home run, and said that his family had rented out a whole section and he could hear them cheering the whole time.

Two areas of his game that White excelled at were his strikeout percentage (17.9%) and his whiff rate (21.9%), both of which rated as well above league average.

His 69.3 mph bat speed ranked tied for 506th out of 619 batters with at least 25 swings. Right next to him on the leaderboard with the same bat speed was Darell Hernaiz, who has also had trouble collecting extra bases.

Alika Williams (69.1 mph) and Jeff McNeil (68.7 mph) are two more bats in that same range, while shortstop Jacob Wilson held the lowest mark on the club at 64.7 mph. There's nothing wrong with White's bat speed being in that group of players unless the expectation is that he'll have more 15-20 home run pop from year to year.

His average exit velocity was also just 85.9 mph, nearly a full three miles per hour below league average (88.6 mph). The lack of consistent bat speed and low exit velocity certainly helped contribute to the lack of power numbers. That said, the power is still expected to come.

In the field White still has some work to do at first base, earning a -1 defensive runs saved grade and then a -3 in both outs above average and fielding run value. At third base, White was actually a plus defender according to DRS, holding a +2. He still came in a little below average with a -3 OAA and a -2 FRV.

The silver lining of the injuries this season is that players like White received legitimate playing time in the big leagues, which provided experience down the roster that otherwise wouldn't have been available. The A's roster is largely set in place with position players, and with Zack Gelof at third and a healthy Nick Kurtz at first base, White may get more seasoning in Triple-A when the season begins.

Even with the potential for a lockout beginning in December, White says he plans to prepare this offseason like there isn't going to be a lockout, which was a common sentiment around the A's clubhouse late in the year.

Before he starts ramping up, the plan is to do some fishing back home in Florida.

articles.title: Simsbury football shuts out Farmington, matching combined win total from past three seasons
articles.summary: Now 4-1, Simsbury scored on its first play from scrimmage and kept Farmington off the scoreboard.
articles.body:
FARMINGTON - An early October victory in Week 5 of the high school football season usually doesn't carry much weight.

That is, unless you're part of the 2026 Simsbury football team. The Trojans' 16-0 CCC win at Farmington was worth documenting.

And the Simsbury seniors did just that before exiting the field Friday night.

On their way back to the locker room with their fourth victory in five weeks, several Trojans made sure to pose in front of the home team's scoreboard.

Why? After three seasons of losing, a 4-1 start matched the win total over those past three seasons.

Prior to going 1-9 last season, the Trojans endured 2-8 and 1-9 campaigns.

"There is just a completely different buy in. Last year, we were 1-9 and that is not what anyone was looking for," Simsbury senior quarterback Braeden Siano said. "Buy in with our new head coach. Buy in with the line. A new coaching staff.

"All together, the line, defense ... I really feel like the buy-in is what's getting us these games," Siano added.

Siano, who started as a junior after moving to Simsbury from Massachusetts, was quick to reference new head coach Jim Caouette - Simsbury's third new man in charge in as many years. Caouette arrived on the scene this year after nine seasons as an assistant at Holy Cross.

Caouette's intensity and attention to detail were apparent all night. His voice was as crisp as the autumn air, echoing across the field until the final seconds ticked off.

"Our kids have bought into the system we are trying to run and our assistant coaches do a wonderful job getting the kids prepared," Caouette said. "I couldn't be happier (to be) 4-1 right now, and where the program is going. We have a lot of things to clean up, but to be 4-1 heading into the bye, I couldn't be happier."

The Trojans never trailed. After holding the River Hawks to a quick three-and-out, Siano hit a streaking Aaron Blecher down the sideline for a 67-yard touchdown on Simsbury's first play.

But after that quick start, it was Simsbury's defense that shined.

The Trojans twice stopped the River Hawks on downs in the first half. They also got an interception from Kayveon Long at their own 30 to stop Farmington's second drive of the game - a 13-play march that included a successful fake punt.

Simsbury was stopped just short of the goal line midway through the second quarter.

But after two runs got Farmington some breathing room, quarterback Mason Kiniry was sacked in the end zone by Long and fellow senior Jesse Carst for a safety and a 9-0 lead for the Trojans.

"When we are out here cooking, making plays and tackling. I'm in the huddle saying, 'Go out there, finishing strong, give me everything you've got,'" said Long. "It's the little things. That's what I've been preaching. We fix those things up and this is the success we get.

"I couldn't ask for anything more," Long added.

Simsbury led 9-0 at halftime. The Trojans took the second-half kickoff 60 yards on seven plays, and Siano found senior Cole Roberts for a 9-yard touchdown pass to make it 16-0 with 8:09 left in the third quarter.

Siano finished 15-of-26 for 213 yards. He was complemented by Nasir Gouldbourne, who ran for 84 yards on 16 carries.

Farmington, enjoying its own resurgence this season, came into the contest averaging 30 points a game, but lost starting quarterback Kiniry to injury.

Sophomore Colton Anderson started the second half behind center and was effective at times. He drove the River Hawks to the Trojans' 13-yard line with 5:12 to play.

But on fourth down, his pass to Tyler McMahon came up short of a first down and the Trojans proceeded to run out the clock.

"You want to learn some things about yourself and who you are ... and still get a victory," Farmington head coach Chris Machol said. "That didn't happen. But I told the kids, they were 3-1 for a reason and we were 3-1 for a reason. I told the guys it would come down to executing plays."

Braeden Siano, Simsbury: The senior quarterback got the Trojans going with a 67-yard touchdown pass on their first play from scrimmage and finished with a pair of TD tosses and 213 yards passing.

"When we needed a stop to keep them out of the end zone, our kids stepped up to the challenge. It was just a good overall defensive effort." - Simsbury head coach Jim Caouette.

articles.title: Takeaways from the Ducks 5-1 Win over the Jets
articles.summary: Lukas Dostal anchored a masterclass in efficiency while a surprising offensive surge from the fourth line propelled Anaheim to a dominant bounce-back victory...
articles.body:
For their first road trip of the 2026-27 season, the Anaheim Ducks set out for a brief two-game-in-two-days trip to Canada to face the Winnipeg Jets on Friday, followed by the Calgary Flames on Saturday.

After winning their first two games of the season, the Ducks suffered their first loss at the hands of the Edmonton Oilers on Wednesday.

The opposing Jets entered the game undefeated in regulation, with a surprising 3-0-1 record on the season. They were without star defenseman Josh Morrissey in this game, who is listed as "day-to-day" with an upper body injury.

Ducks head coach Joel Quenneville shuffled several of his lines and pairs, as he's want to do after losses, and especially losses where multiple lines need a jolt. The only forward line to remain intact from Wednesday was the fourth line and the only defense pair untouched was the middle pair.

Here's how the Ducks lined up to start this game:

Lukas Dostal got the start for the Ducks for the fourth time in four games to open the season and stopped 15 of 16 shots. He was opposed by Clay Stevenson in the Winnipeg crease, who saved 12 of 16.

This was far and away the Ducks' tightest-checking, low-event game of the season and likely such in recent memory. However, it was less sloppy and more efficient an effort, as they were opportunistic on the rush, where all five of their goals were scored, and they allowed virtually no inside looks for Winnipeg and cleared any second-chance opportunities.

Fourth Line : Scoring two of the Ducks' five goals was their consistent fourth line. They did everything expected of a modern NHL fourth line in this game: provided energy, displayed responsible defense, pressured heavily on the forecheck, etc.

However, when they won possession of the puck, they operated like an excellent top-nine line in this game. They were reading how plays were breaking, carried pucks smartly and skillfully through neutral ice with speed, and revealed a finishing quality that's rare among players in their roles.

Washe was disruptive on the defensive end and drove cycles, Mallot showed surprising IQ, speed, and vision with the puck on his stick, and Caulfield made stickhandles and passes under opposing sticks all game.

The Ducks needed to find depth scoring from somewhere, and the fourth line, the last place one would expect to find it, delivered masterfully.

Noah Warren : Warren finished the Ducks' game against the Oilers alongside star defenseman Jackson LaCombe, where he played the entirety of this game. He logged 24:12 TOI, including 5:16 on the penalty kill, where he was a significant contributor to the Ducks killing all four penalties they took.

Warren didn't miss a beat with his promotion, and provided not only "stay at home" support for LaCombe, but he proved remarkably effective with his mobility, more akin to a modern-day shutdown defenseman. As mentioned, he covered a lot of ice on the defensive side of the puck with his stride and reach, greatly and rapidly minimizing time and space for his opponent.

Even on the occasional misread, he recovered remarkably well and was able to disrupt multiple attacks singlehandedly. His puck-moving was simple, but effective, as he was equal parts careful and decisive.

Breakouts : As a whole, the Ducks breakouts were much more simplified in this game. Defensemen weren't quick to settle for rimming pucks to open half walls. Instead, if they were unable to make a tape-to-tape outlet, they resorted to high flips or glass-chips into neutral ice, so as to punt an ensuing battle to neutral instead of deep in the defensive zone.

Forwards, especially lower in the lineup, were similarly elementary with their second touches and more willing to chase down and pressure opponents who attained possession.

Beckett Sennecke : Sennecke's 365-day evolution from turnover-prone rookie to bona fide play-driving sophomore will go a long way toward mitigating what the Ducks' depth chart lost over the offseason. One of his biggest strengths coming out of junior was his ability to read how pucks bounce out of battles and how to manufacture puck touches for himself at full speed.

He's translating that element of his game seamlessly just 86 games into his career. He's understanding his limitations at the NHL level, limiting his propensity for risky plays. Sennecke is attacking the game rather than letting it come to him and operating at breakneck speed. He's singlehandedly dictating the flow of play and not only reading and manipulating single defenders one-on-one, but entire opposing defensive structures. He's playing like a true superstar winger four games into this young season.

The Ducks will have a quick turnaround, as they'll travel to Calgary to face the Flames on Saturday at 7 pm PST.

articles.title: ‘Ring us already’ – Fans react as Atlanta Dream sweep Liberty to reach first WNBA Finals since 2013
articles.summary: Atlanta Dream fans are already looking ahead to the WNBA Finals after their team swept the New York Liberty 3-0 to reach the championship series for the firs...
articles.body:
Atlanta Dream fans are already looking ahead to the WNBA Finals after their team swept the New York Liberty 3-0 to reach the championship series for the first time since 2013.

The Dream held on for an 85-83 victory at Barclays Center on Friday night as Angel Reese scored 22 points and Jordin Canada added 19 points and 11 assists.

Atlanta will now face the winner of the Las Vegas Aces and Golden State Valkyries series in the Finals. The Dream have also won 10 straight games heading into the championship round.

Atlanta Dream fans are already demanding a championship

There was plenty of excitement among Dream supporters following the historic victory with several fans already calling for the franchise to finish the job.

One supporter wrote: "Give us the ring already." Another added: "Ring us already, no one even comes close to us."

The confidence was balanced by one fan who reminded the team that there is still work to do: "Job isn't finished. One more series to go!"

Another supporter was already looking ahead to the four wins needed for the championship: "Four more wins, Dream. Please keep that aggressiveness and get that ring."

The team effort was also praised after Atlanta held off a late Liberty push.

"Yes, great team win. Everyone did their job and played a part. So proud of you all. Way to stick together and bring it home. Clutch free throws by DB, huge three from JC," one fan wrote.

Another supporter shared the same excitement: "So proud of this incredible team! Y'all fought so hard to get here, and now it's time to bring that championship home!"

Reese also received plenty of praise after another huge playoff performance, with one fan noting: "Angel Reese has never lost a WNBA playoff game in her life."

Another supporter went even further with their celebration: "State Farm Arena belongs to the Dream from now on."

Atlanta now has a chance to end the franchise's wait for its first WNBA championship when the Finals begin on October 17.

articles.title: High school football: Best of Friday’s action, from team of the week to top player performances
articles.summary: Recapping the best of what took place in Friday’s Week 6 of high school football in the East Metro and beyond. Team of the night: Mounds View The Mustangs us...
articles.body:
Recapping the best of what took place in Friday's Week 6 of high school football in the East Metro and beyond.

The Mustangs used a 5-yard rushing score from Connor Jude to edge Woodbury, 14-13 , in a pivotal Metro East subdistrict tilt on Friday.

The Mounds View defense surrendered a touchdown on Woodbury's opening drive, but didn't surrender another offensive point all evening.

With the win, the Mustangs remained perfect in subdistrict play. They'll square off with Forest Lake in the bout that's likely to determine the subdistrict title and No. 1 seed in the Class 6A playoffs next week.

Burnsville: The Blaze earned their first win of the season Friday, edging Apple Valley 27-26.

New Richmond: The Tigers sewed up the Big Rivers Conference title with a 49-21 win over Menomonie. New Richmond dominated the conference slate, winning every game but one by three-plus scores.

Player of the night: Colton Butts, White Bear Lake wide receiver

Butts tallied six grabs for 157 yards and three scores in the Bears' dramatic, 32-29 win over Stillwater. Two of those touchdowns came in the final frame, including the game-winning 20-yard receiving touchdown with 34 seconds to play.

Wyatt Stachowiak, White Bear Lake quarterback: It was splitting hairs selecting between Butts and Stachowiak for the top honor, but hat tip to the signal caller for throwing for 289 yards and four scores in a win that will go a long way toward netting the Bears a home playoff game.

Braden Hatalla, Stillwater quarterback: It came in a losing effort, but Hatalla was wonderful on Friday. The Ponies' signal caller accumulated nearly 300 yards of total offense, including 153 yards and three scores on the ground.

Carter Cupito, SMB quarterback: Yes, the quarterback is the son of former Gophers QB Bryan Cupito. But Carter, a multi-sport athlete at Minnehaha Academy, is making a name for himself.

The freshman, who already has an offer from the Gophers, threw for six more touchdowns in SMB's 56-0 win over Concordia Academy to keep the Wolfpack unbeaten. Cupito has 23 passing touchdowns through six games.

Frank Schwieters, Mahtomedi defensive back: The senior hauled in two interceptions in the Zephyrs' 27-3 win over Tartan, including one he returned for a touchdown in the second quarter.

Mack Jurkovich, Forest Lake running back: The Rangers' star runner scored thrice more in Forest Lake's 44-27 win over East Ridge.

Eli Larson, St. Croix Lutheran running back: Larson tallied touchdown runs of 43, 50, 52 and 58 yards in the Crusaders' 42-20 win over St. Agnes.

Play of the night: Burnsville's defensive stop

Apple Valley scored with eight minutes to play to trim Burnsville's lead to 27-26. The Eagles elected to go for two and the lead. But quarterback Noah Weaver's attempted bootleg was immediately snuffed out by a blitzing Donnavon Lyons to blow up the attempt and preserve a lead that held through the finish line.

Moorhead won the battle of the Class 6A titans, topping Eden Prairie 55-34. The Gophers commitment passing combo of Jett Feeney (quarterback) and David Mack (receiver) was again firing on all cylinders. Feeney threw for 372 yards and six scores, five of which went to Mack.

Moorhead and Champlin Park and now the lone two unbeatens remaining in Class 6A after Shakopee was knocked off 14-10 by Prior Lake in a stunning upset. It's just the Lakers' second win of the season.

There are seven one-loss teams in the state's biggest class.

River Falls clinched its playoff spot via a 24-8 win over Rice Lake. Menomonie will need to upset River Falls next week in its regular season finale to guarantee itself a place in the playoff field. Hudson, New Richmond and Chippewa Falls are all also locked into the playoffs from the Big Rivers Conference.

In the Middle Border Conference, Somerset and St. Croix Central will square off in a win-and-in contest, where the loser will hope to qualify with a losing conference record. Amery can secure a playoff spot with a win over Prescott, while Osceola and Baldwin-Woodville will play next week for the conference crown.

articles.title: Bruins Trade Pitch Lands Dylan Larkin, Sending $19 Million Veteran to Red Wings
articles.summary: A Bruins trade proposal would bring Red Wings ex-captain Dylan Larkin to Boston in exchange for a $19 million veteran. Here's how. The post Bruins Trade Pitc...
articles.body:
Dylan Larkin asked the Detroit Red Wings for a trade, lost the captaincy over it — and still plays for Detroit anyway. But now, a new trade pitch aimed at the Boston Bruins would take Larkin out of Detroit, as he wants, and land him with another Original Six squad.

The trade pitch published late Friday on PuckGM would ship Larkin to Boston for Pavel Zacha, William Moore's signing rights and a 2027 first-round pick. Would that deal end the standoff?

Larkin, 30, grew up in Waterford, Michigan, and has never worn another NHL sweater. Detroit drafted him 15th overall in 2014 after he piled up 47 points in 35 games at the University of Michigan, according to NHL.com's Dylan Larkin player profile. He entered this season 10th in franchise history with 643 points in 808 games, and he scored 34 goals and 67 points in 74 games last year.

Dylan Larkin Trade Request Standoff With Detroit Red Wings

Larkin's eight-year contract pays $8.7 million annually through 2030-31 and includes a full no-trade clause through 2027-28, according to PuckPedia's contract breakdown for Larkin.

Then came June. Sportsnet 's Elliotte Friedman reported June 4 that Larkin wanted out. Steve Yzerman, then Detroit's general manager, confirmed June 27 that Larkin's agent had supplied a short list of teams that Larkin would go to.

"My job as the manager of the Detroit Red Wings is always to do what is in the best interest of the Detroit Red Wings, and I will act accordingly to that," Yzerman said, as quoted by NHL.com columnist Nicholas J. Cotsonika .

Larkin held the captaincy from January 2021 until this fall. The Red Wings opened the season without one.

"I asked for a trade from the Detroit Red Wings as the captain, and actions have consequences," Larkin said, according to NHL.com . He is playing for Detroit regardless.

Zacha, 29, was born in Brno, Czech Republic. New Jersey drafted him sixth overall in 2015 and traded him to Boston in July 2022. He set career highs of 30 goals and 65 points in 78 games last season and owns 407 points in 710 career games . His $4.75 million contract expires after this season.

Moore, 19, a center from Mississauga, Ontario, went 51st overall to Boston in 2025 out of the U.S. National Team Development Program. He plays at Boston College and remains unsigned. Scouts project the 6-foot-2 playmaker as a middle-six forward who must add strength, according to an Elite Prospects scouting report .

Would Bruins and Red Wings Weigh a Dylan Larkin Trade Package?

The cap ledger favors Detroit in the trade pitch on the PuckGM table. Boston would absorb roughly $3.95 million in added cap hit, Larkin's $8.7 million replacing Zacha's $4.75 million, with its projected total already near $101.5 million, according to PuckGM's cap projection for the Bruins roster . Detroit clears that same $3.95 million and adds a prospect and a pick at no cap cost.

The lineup favors Boston. The Bruins have sought a true No. 1 center since Patrice Bergeron retired in 2023, and Elias Lindholm, Fraser Minten, James Hagens, Casey Mittelstadt and Zacha have not filled the role, according to an analysis by The Athletic . Detroit loses its most consistent center, though Larkin outscored Zacha by only four goals and two points last season, in four fewer games.

The obstacle is the no-trade clause. Larkin's reported list started with Florida, Minnesota and Vegas, according to a Detroit Free Press report . It has since grown to include Colorado, Washington, Dallas and Tampa Bay, according to a newer report by Sportsnet . The name Bruins has not cropped up.

Interim general manager Shawn Horcoff has set no timeline.

"We're going to take this day by day," Horcoff has said. For now, Larkin keeps skating in Detroit.

articles.title: Prince Harry booed as Leicester roar back to beat Gloucester
articles.summary: The royal was a surprise attendee at the Prem Rugby clash at Mattioli Woods Welford Road
articles.body:
Prince Harry watched on as Leicester Tigers roared back to beat Gloucester in a thrilling Gallagher Prem clash.

The visitors roared into a 14-0 lead at Mattioli Woods Welford Road as Leicester were reduced to 14 men in the first 10 minutes with fly half Billy Searle shown a yellow card.

But Tigers dominated much of what followed thereafter with a powerful performance from their pack, with tries from forwards Finn Carnduff, Joe Heyes, Jamie Blamire and Aaron Wainwright.

Ollie Hassell-Collins made certain of victory with a fine finish in the left corner late on – though Gloucester, who had won their first two games of the season, snatched two potentially valuable bonus points with a late rally.

"We can't start games like we are at the moment," Leicester boss Geoff Parling said after the 38-31 win. "We've not started well in games repeatedly this season so first 10 minutes, a 14-0 lead [for Gloucester] but I didn't feel like we'd thrown a punch, so I felt very calm there.

"There were some really good bits in the rest of the game. They've got multiple threats around the ball – like Jac Morgan , Dewi Lake – and I thought our carrying was excellent, I felt the way we applied pressure through our defence, you're starting to see it come through more in how we want that to be.

"We did some really good stuff and we actually feel a bit deflated at the end of the game after giving them those two bonus points, but I think that's a sign of the desire of the team. We've got five points and a big performance against a team that's been going well."

The Duke of Sussex was a surprise attendee at the game at Welford Road – though his image appeared to be booed by some when displayed on the big screen. Mike Tindall, married to Harry's cousin Zara, is a former Gloucester captain.

Leicester's success meant they retain the Slater Cup – a trophy that honours former Gloucester and Tigers lock Ed Slater , who retired in 2022 after being diagnosed with Motor Neurone Disease (MND).
