articles.title: Injured Wautoma football player experiences senior night while recovering from severe concussion
articles.summary: WAUTOMA, Wis. (WFRV) – Senior night on Friday didn’t unfold the way Dom Rooney had envisioned it would when he began his final year as a member of the Wautom...
articles.body:
WAUTOMA, Wis. (WFRV) - Senior night on Friday didn't unfold the way Dom Rooney had envisioned it would when he began his final year as a member of the Wautoma Hornets football team.

But, given the circumstances, it was still a special night for Dom and his family.

"His face lights up, he loves the support," Dom's mom Kimberly Kozlowski told Local 5 News. "He loves to know that people he doesn't even know are rallying around him."

There were serious questions about whether or not he'd be able to be at senior night with his teammates. During Wautoma's football game last week, Dom suffered a serious concussion and had to be airlifted to Children's Wisconsin in Milwaukee.

Doctors discharged him from the hospital just a few days ago. He can't walk or talk, but with the help of his friends and family he was able to be at senior night on Friday with his teammates.

"It makes him stronger, it makes him push through, and it just means the world to us, it means everything," Kozlowski said.

The community has rallied around Dom and his family since the injury. 'Dom Strong' shirts filled the sideline and the bleachers. Some of the proceeds from t-shirt sales have gone to support Dom's family with the recovery process. There was also a 50-50 rally on Friday night to help the family and several local organizations and businesses have also raised or donated money.

Dom can't speak, but used a whiteboard to write down a message to all of his supporters.

"I hope they realize how meaningful their words and actions are," he wrote.

Dom's mom said the's beginning physical and speech therapy and while it will likely be a long road to recovery, they're seeing small improvements every day.

articles.title: WNBA playoff winners and losers include Dream's Jordin Canada, Liberty coach
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries have punched their tickets to the WNBA Finals. Here are the semifinal winners and losers.
articles.body:
We will have first-time WNBA champion in 2026.

The Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries have punched their tickets to the WNBA Finals. Neither team has won a title. The Dream lost in their only WNBA Finals appearance in 2013. The Valkyries joined the league in 2025 as an expansion franchise.

The beat the 2024 WNBA champion New York Liberty 85-83 on Friday to complete a semifinal sweep.

To secure their spot against the Dream, the No. 2 seeded Valkyries beat the Las Vegas Aces 87-77 on Friday, Oct. 9, at Michelob Ultra Arena in Game 3 of the WNBA playoff semifinals.

The WNBA Finals begin Oct. 17. Here are the Game 3 semifinals winners and losers.

Liberty, Dream and Aces, Valkyries in WNBA semifinal playoff action

Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese helped Atlanta punch its ticket to the franchise's first WNBA Finals appearance since 2013.

Reese finished with 22 points, nine rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal in the closeout win, shooting 7-18 from the field, 2-of-4 from the 3-point line and a perfect 6-of-6 from the free-throw line in 37 minutes.

It'll be the first WNBA Finals appearance of Reese's budding career. But she knew she would be here, well before the 6-foot-4 forward was traded to the Dream in April after two seasons with the Chicago Sky. Almost a year to the day on Oct. 11, 2025, Reese tweeted , "Manifesting the finals."

"I manifested this. When I came to Atlanta, I knew that I was getting," Reese said. "This team has poured so much into me. We poured so much into each other. I posted and tweeted (on) 10/10/25 that I was manifesting the Finals and this is my moment. I'm supposed to be here. I thank God for this moment. And I'm just so thankful."

Reese, who set single-season records for the most rebounds (521) and double-doubles (32) in a single season, has averaged 18.0 points, 8.4 rebounds and 2.2 blocks in five games in the 2026 postseason as the Dream extend their win streak to 10 games in a row row, dating back to the regular season.

Jordin Canada owning the series against the Liberty

Dream guard Jordin Canada was an absolute dawg against the Liberty, owning the series from the first tip. In three games, Canada averaged 22.3 points on 62.3%, 7.6 assists, three rebounds and two steals. She punctuated her amazing semifinals run with a 19-point double-double which included 11 assists. She became the third player in WNBA history to record at least 11 assists with zero turnovers in a playoff series-clinching game. Canada joins Cynthia Cooper and Diana Taurasi as the only players to achieve this milestone.

"When I went in the huddle, I said we're gonna have to earn it. This is a really good (Liberty) team. ...They're going to fight 'til the end. And so, we just got to want it more. We got to bring that energy. We gotta play Atlanta Dream basketball," Canada said of the Dream being down two to enter the fourth quarter.

"We did an exceptional job of getting stops when we needed (them) most, getting timely buckets when we needed it most, and just being poised and composed in that moment. And I know that also starts with me."

Golden State Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase may have missed out on 2026 WNBA Coach of the Year (which went to Minnesota Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve), but her team's success in their second year of existence shows she is deserving.

Nakase led the Valkyries to the playoffs in their inaugural season in 2025, becoming the first expansion team to make the postseason. Golden State took it a step further in Year 2 and punched their ticket to the WNBA Finals by sweeping out the defending champion Las Vegas Aces.

"We're a team that just believes in one another. We believe in what we have here, and I think it's showing on the court time and time again, no matter what happens, what's thrown our way, we trust in each other," said Veronica Burton, who finished with eight points, six rebounds and four assists. "This is a dream come true."

Aces head coach Becky Hammon said Nakase has her "club playing at a really high level all year." Nakase previously served as an assistant coach for the Aces under Hammon (2022-24) and was part of the team's 2022 and 2023 WNBA championships.

Everyone who wanted A'ja Wilson or Breanna Stewart in the Finals

For the first time since 2021, neither A'ja Wilson nor Breanna Stewart will be in the WNBA Finals. Wilson and Stewart have effectively run the league during the last five years. Wilson and the Las Vegas Aces won three of the last four championships (2022, 2023, 2025). Stewart and the Liberty won the other (2024).

Now, this year's Finals won't have either. Anyone who wanted to see Wilson and Stewart, we're so sorry, friends. This isn't the year. The latest WNBA Finals matchup between the Dream and Valkyries shows how parity is increasing in the league. The Dream and the Valkyries finished fourth and second in the standings, respectively, but they played like the best two teams in the postseason. Could this be a changing of the guard?

Chris DeMarco's first season as the head coach of the New York Liberty came to an unceremonious end on Friday with the Liberty being swept.

There were some questionable choices made throughout the series, none more than the reset timeout that wasn't used with 4.3 seconds left in the Liberty's Game 2 loss on Wednesday.

Breanna Stewart said she was told by officials New York didn't have a reset timeout when she inquired during Angel Reese's free throw attempts. Officials countered Stewart's claim in the postgame pool report, saying the referee confirmed New York did have one. The Liberty submitted an official inquiry into the timeout situation with the league, a person familiar with the situation told USA TODAY.

DeMarco said he expects to return as the head coach next year. The Liberty's Big 3 of Breanna Stewart, Sabrina Ionescu and Jonquel Jones were asked the same question, with each player mentioning that it's not up to them.

"We want to win a championship every single time we step on the court, but it's really hard in this league. And in order to do that, you need to be consistent for the full 44 games," said Breana Stewart, who finished with 26 points and six assists. "I don't think we were consistent throughout the season... It's not like cramming for a test. You gotta you gotta be ready to go since the jump."

It's worth mentioning the Liberty battled injuries throughout the season. Ionesco was limited to 31 regular-season games due to injury, Leonie Fiebich played 21 and Satou Sabally 13 games before shutting down her season.

"I think we navigated it well. I think especially Satou (Sabally), she's built for a series like this, obviously, with her ability to be physical, get to the rim, do all those things," DeMarco said. "But again, and not to go down that path, but the priority with her is always going to be health. We want to make sure she feels good before she plays again."

The Las Vegas Aces and New York Liberty each found themselves in a 2-0 hole in their respective semifinal series. But each team had a chance to get in the win column and keep their season alive on their home courts. Yet, the Aces and Liberty both got swept in Las Vegas and New York, respectively.

Valkyries forward Gabby Williams even said Michelob ULTRA Arena felt like a home game.

"I was getting a little bit emotional walking off the court with our fans because I know how much they have our back and they really ride for us," Williams said. "I wanted for us to continue to have a shot and extend this season and play for our fans.

"The ones that have been here really know how much they mean to us."

articles.title: WSU Goes Scoreless in Second Half, Falls to Utah State, 17-16
articles.summary: Washington State and Utah State both entered the game with 1-4 records. Utah State would come out victorious, leaving the Cougars alone at 1-5 at the bottom...
articles.body:
Washington State and Utah State both entered the game with 1-4 records. Utah State would come out victorious, leaving the Cougars alone at 1-5 at the bottom of the Pac-12 standings.

WSU kicked the ball off to the Aggies to open the game. The kick was short, and Utah State returner Noah White couldn't secure the ball, allowing the Cougars to recover it at the Utah State 25-yard line

The Cougar offense started with a handoff to Tank Hawkins that went backwards for a loss of two. After an incomplete pass and a third-down run with Maxwell Woods for no gain, WSU sent out kicker Jack Stevens to attempt a 40-yard field goal. Stevens was true from 40 yards to give WSU an early 3-0 lead.

Utah State got the ball back, and after a pass interference flag kept the drive moving, the Cougar defense got its first third-down stop of the game, forcing a 38-yard Utah State field goal miss. WSU was able to hold on to its 3-0 lead.

After struggling with time of possession all year, the WSU offense was able to put together a 15-play, 9:20 drive, a welcome change for the WSU defense. The drive saw some creative play calling from Kirby Moore, including a Caden Pinnick fake pitch to Kirby Voorhees to pick up a third-and-short. Holding calls ended up stalling the drive, and the Cougar offense settled for a 43-yard Stevens field goal to take a 6-0 lead with 1:02 left in the first quarter.

The Aggies' second drive was sparked by a 33-yard deep pass to Eli Wood to set the Aggies up in Cougar territory to begin the second quarter. Thankfully for the Cougars, the Aggies didn't go much further, as they had to settle for a 48-yard field goal to make it a 6-3 game.

WSU got the ball back, and after an eight-play, 43-yard drive, Stevens was sent out for a 50-yard field goal attempt. He made the kick to push the Cougar lead to 9-3, and Stevens was officially on fire!

After the teams traded punts, the Aggies decided to gamble on 4th and 3 from midfield. Quarterback Grady Broserhous tried to scramble for it but was stopped just short of the line to gain. WSU picked up a big fourth-down stop and started with the ball at their own 47-yard line. The Cougar offense couldn't do much with the golden opportunity, as a holding call led to a third-and-long, eventually resulting in a third-down sack. Luckily for the Cougs, Utah State was flagged for an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty to keep the WSU drive alive and give WSU a fresh set of downs.

On the very next play, the WSU offensive line opened up a massive hole for Leo Pulalsi to score a 54-yard touchdown on the ground, giving WSU a 16-3 lead.

Both teams again traded punts heading into halftime, and Moore and the Cougs went into the break with a 16-3 lead and all the momentum. It felt like the offense, while stagnant at times, looked slightly more competent with Moore behind the wheel of the ship.

The WSU offense opened the third quarter with a quick three-and-out, a familiar theme for a WSU team that has been slow to start coming out of halftime.

Linus Zunk and the defense were able to force their own three-and-out, as Zunk picked up a sack on third down to return the ball right back to Pinnick and the offense.

After looking like they had regained some positive momentum, the offense ran a fake end-around, Pinnick kept the ball, and he fumbled it, giving the ball right back to the Aggies in prime field position at the WSU 39-yard line.

The turnover would instantly come back to bite them, as Utah State responded with a 27-yard touchdown catch. The Utah State receiver appeared to bobble the ball before securing it out of bounds, but the officials decided not to officially review the play, and the touchdown stood. WSU's lead was now cut to just six points at 16-10.

After Pinnick's legs kept the following drive alive on a 3rd and 7, Maxwell Woods appeared to have gashed the Aggie defense with a 37-yard run, but the play was called back for an illegal shift to erase the big gain. WSU again faced a third down, but Pinnick's legs couldn't pick up a first down, as he was taken down for a sack and WSU was forced to punt the ball back to the Aggies.

A tackle for loss and a sack forced a Utah State three-and-out, again giving the ball back to the WSU offense with a chance to take back a two-possession lead.

On the first play of the drive, a Darious Clemmens first-down catch, combined with a late hit out of bounds, got WSU all the way to the 50-yard line. The offense was unable to capitalize after the play and again punted the ball back to Utah State.

The Cougar defense gave up an explosive 41-yard completion to Demick Starling to open the first Aggie drive of the 4th quarter, but the Aggie offense stalled out after Aggie head coach Bronco Mendenhall was flagged for a 15-yard unsportsmanlike conduct, knocking the Aggies out of field goal range and again giving the ball back to the WSU offense.

After another long run was called back for a hold, WSU was forced into a third down. Jack Pedersen caught the ball well short of the first-down marker but fumbled it. It was the second fumble of the half, and Utah State had the ball back at the WSU 19-yard line.

Three plays later, Utah State was in the end zone, and WSU was trailing for the first time, 17-16, with 6:22 left in the game.

Stop me if you've heard this before, but the following drive by the Cougar offense was again another three-and-out, giving the ball right back to Utah State. The defense was able to force a third-and-2 at the Utah State 46-yard line. Utah State came up about six inches short but decided to kick the ball away to a sputtering Cougar offense.

The Cougar offense would have one more chance to put up its first points of the second half.

The first play of the drive started with Pinnick running into a sack, followed by an incomplete pass. On third down, Pinnick rolled to his right and found an open Pedersen for a first down. However, two flags were sitting back at the line of scrimmage, and another offensive holding call wiped away a positive play for the Cougars.

WSU came out of the two-minute timeout facing a 3rd and 24, and it couldn't convert, punting the ball in the hands of Utah State with 1:43 remaining.

Utah State was able to ice the game away with a 12-yard run up the middle on 2nd and 9 to send the Cougars to 1-5.

It continues WSU's worst start since they started 1-9 in the 2010 season. They finished that season 2-10.

Moore and the team will have some major soul-searching to do before heading to Corvallis for a 3 p.m. kickoff against a seemingly rejuvinated Beavers team on Saturday, October 17th.

articles.title: Boone Jenner’s ‘gusty’ review of Capitals’ intense win over Rangers
articles.summary: The Washington Capitals defeated the New York Rangers on Friday night. It was an intense game between two Metropolitan Division rivals. It’s early in the sea...
articles.body:
The Washington Capitals defeated the New York Rangers on Friday night. It was an intense game between two Metropolitan Division rivals. It's early in the season, but there is certainly no love lost between these teams. In the end, it was one of the newer Capitals, Boone Jenner, who made the difference.

Jenner took advantage of a New York turnover to bury the game-winning goal in the second period. It was his first goal as a member of the Capitals, as well. Washington finished out a tough 3-1 win on home ice thanks to that goal.

"Doesn't matter what time of year, obviously when they're in the division, they're a little bit bigger," Jenner said after the game , via NHL.com. "But at the end of the day you need to collect points, and I think it was a gutsy way to close out that game and make sure we got them."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Jenner is in the midst of his first season with the Capitals . He signed with Washington as a free agent over the summer. Prior to that, he spent his entire career with the Columbus Blue Jackets. Jenner spent the last five seasons as the captain of the Blue Jackets.

The Rangers lost a big piece of their puzzle in this game. Igor Shesterkin left the contest in the second period with a lower-body injury. He had to be helped off the ice and was unable to put weight on his leg. The Rangers had no update on his condition after the game.

The Capitals have now won two games in a row. Washington will look to make it three in a row on Sunday when they take on the Seattle Kraken.

articles.title: Liberty’s Chris DeMarco celebrates NY players for fighting hard vs. Dream
articles.summary: The New York Liberty saw their postseason end earlier than hoped after falling 85-83 to the Atlanta Dream in Game 3 on Friday, completing a three-game sweep...
articles.body:
The New York Liberty saw their postseason end earlier than hoped after falling 85-83 to the Atlanta Dream in Game 3 on Friday, completing a three-game sweep in the WNBA semifinals.

The defeat came less than two weeks after the Liberty made history by becoming the first No. 8 seed to eliminate a No. 1 seed in the playoffs. Their upset of the Minnesota Lynx earned them a second-round matchup with Atlanta, but they could not extend their run against the younger Dream squad.

Despite the disappointment, head coach Chris DeMarco had no shortage of praise for his players , as he remained focused on the effort his team showed throughout the series.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"I want to say our players fought like hell," DeMarco said. "They played so hard, and whether it was getting out of that first round to have the chance to play in this one, or was just these three games. Like I'm so proud of our players and how hard they played."

New York had opportunities to force another game but could not make the decisive plays late. Breanna Stewart missed a potential game-tying shot in the closing seconds, while DeWanna Bonner converted two free throws after drawing a foul to help Atlanta secure the win.

Stewart finished with 26 points on 6-of-15 shooting, while Jonquel Jones also scored 26 points and grabbed 14 rebounds. Their performances were not enough to overcome Atlanta's late push, led by Jordin Canada, who recorded 13 points and 11 assists. Angel Reese added 22 points and nine rebounds for the Dream.

The loss leaves New York facing another offseason after its first-round exit in 2025. For now, the Liberty must process another missed championship opportunity after a playoff run that began with one of the franchise's biggest upsets.

articles.title: Running back Ayden Fernandez carries red hot Reagan to win against Madison
articles.summary: The two-way athlete had his best game of the season at running back, rushing for 189 yards and two touchdowns to lead the Rattlers over the Mavericks.
articles.body:
Reagan's bolt of offensive energy has come across the ball from all-district linebacker Ayden Fernandez.

Fernandez delivered his best performance of the season Friday with 189 yards and two touchdowns on 23 carries in the Rattlers' 21-9 victory against Madison at Comalander Stadium.

"I feel it's the biggest cheat code you can have," Fernandez said. "I mean, as a linebacker, you're taught to guess where the running back is. I use that to my advantage as best I can, hitting the holes and manipulating them like I would to running back."

Reagan improved to 3-2 overall and 3-0 in District 28-6A, which is tied with No. 1 Johnson (5-0, 3-0) in the standings.

Fernandez scored on touchdown runs of 12 and 33 yards to give him seven rushing scores for the season. It was his best performance since going for 197 yards in a victory against Roosevelt last year.

"In practice, we have one motto - downhill run, downhill run," Fernandez said. "As you see, downhill running works. When you hit the gap fast, hit the hole fast, good things happen. When the o-linemen are on their keys, good things happen."

Fernandez is providing what the Rattlers needed on the offensive end after struggling in non-district losses against Steele (52-21) and Brennan (63-0) to open the season.

"He really created the spark we needed," Reagan coach Preston Meyer said. "We didn't really run the ball very well early, and he's come over there and he's really provided that spark. The kids look to him and has those leadership qualities and has done a really good job."

In district play, Fernandez has relinquished most of his defensive duties to focus on offense. It's a role he loves to play.

"It's a blessing," Fernandez said. "How many people in 6A Texas football get to say they play both sides - offense and defense - and make a big impact? I have faith in the guys, and I have faith in my team. One out of 11. Every eleven has to do his job."

Following a scoreless first quarter, Madison broke on the scoreboard midway through the second with a 35-yard field goal by Richard Manning. The score was set up by Juan Gonzalez's interception on Madison's 7-yard line that stopped a promising drive.

Reagan answered on the ensuing possession when Fernandez scored on a 12-yard touchdown run, capping a seven-play, 48-yard drive. Reagan's Ben Rice returned a kickoff 36 yards to put the Rattlers in Madison territory.

The Ratters that 7-3 lead into intermission and made it 14-3 on Fernandez's 33-yard score with 8:01 in the third.

Madison pulled to within 14-9 on Elijah Brito's 14-yard score. The Mavericks made the extra point but took it off the board and elected to go for two when Reagan was called for an offside penalty. The Mavericks missed on the running try.

Madison made a final push for the win and got to Reagan's 9-yard line with less than a minute left on a hook and lateral to Jaleel Lowery, who pitched to Decoreion McMillan for 33 yards. Two plays later, Jaden Bullock returned an interception 94 yards for a touchdown that sealed the game.

articles.title: Arizona volleyball drops 3-setter to No. 8 TCU
articles.summary: Britt Carlson had a solid match in her first extended playing time
articles.body:
When a volleyball team gets outhit, outblocked, and outdug, it's not a surprise to lose in straight sets in less than 90 minutes. The Arizona Wildcats had that experience against No. 8 TCU in Fort Worth, Tex. on Friday afternoon. The Horned Frogs kept their conference record perfect in a 3-0 (25-17, 25-23, 25-20) victory.

If there's a silver lining for the Wildcats, it's that they came back and were competitive in the final two sets after a slow start. The Horned Frogs had a very easy first set victory, but Arizona pushed them after that.

Wildcats head coach Rita Stubbs was creative with her personnel, as she has often been this year. It helped the team compete, but it wasn't enough to pull off an upset that's desperately needed.

Stubbs subbed in freshman outside hitter Hayden Reeder for Destiny Ndam-Simpson fairly early in the match. That helped stabilize serve receive. She also put in senior opposite Britt Carlson , who started the season with an injury. Carlson made her first appearance of the year last week, but she got more play this time around.

When Carlson entered the match, Stubbs also made a change in which opposite and setter were paired together in the Wildcats' 6-2 system. She typically starts with Maria Olga Siapani at setter and Kennedy Osunsanmi on the right side. Harmony Sample comes in to set with Renee Jones at opposite when Siapani is ready to rotate to the front row.

Beginning in the second set, it was Osunsanmi and Sample on the court to start things off. Siapani and Carlson subbed in later.

The changes helped Arizona's offense. After getting just eight kills against six errors in the first set, the Wildcats had 14 kills in the second and 13 in the third. It cut a seven-kill disadvantage in the first set to just one in the second and none in the third.

The loss in the first set was quickly put behind them. Arizona had fallen into a 4-0 deficit in the first set. In the second, the Wildcats were the ones out to a 4-1 lead. When the lead grew to 11-7, TCU head coach Jason Williams called time.

His team responded. TCU put together a 5-1 run to tie the set at 12. Its first lead came at 13-12.

Arizona didn't surrender but it couldn't take the advantage again. The final tie in the second was at 23 points apiece. TCU grabbed the next two points to go up 2-0 in the match.

The Wildcats got another slow start in the final set, falling behind 4-1. Once again, they fought back. TCU could never out more than three points between the two teams, and Arizona eventually tied it at 17-17. That was the last stand for the visitors, who fell to 6-9 overall and 1-3 in the Big 12.

The Wildcats were led by Carlson with seven kills on .316 hitting. Her two total blocks gave her eight points. She also had an assist.

Carlie Cisneros was second on the team in points with seven. She earned them on five kills, one ace, and two total blocks.

Arizona has another challenging match on Sunday. They were set to travel to Waco, Tex. after the game against TCU. They will practice at Baylor on Saturday then face the Bears at noon MST on Sunday.

Baylor has an RPI of 20 and is receiving votes in the AVCA poll. Arizona is searching for a big upset to help its RPI of 137. Based on the unofficial RPI that was used earlier in the year, the Wildcats have climbed about 60 spots since conference play started despite losing three of four. It is still searching for a win against a top 50 team and is 2-7 against teams in the top 100.

articles.title: Ronaldo returns after Portugal quarrel to score in Al-Nassr win
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo opened the scoring for Al-Nassr in their 3-0 win over Diriyah, his first game since Portugal walkout.
articles.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo returned to club football action on Friday after a controversial international break with Portugal and scored the opening goal as Al-Nassr beat Diriyah 3-0 in the Saudi Pro League.

The victory put the defending champions level on points behind leader Al-Qadsiah on goal difference in the eighth round.

During the international window, the 41-year-old Ronaldo walked out of the Portugal squad, for which he has scored 146 goals in 234 appearances.

In a long statement posted on Tuesday, Ronaldo said Portugal coach Jorge Jesus had not been true to his word about when he would play the striker in the Nations League.

Ronaldo won the Saudi Arabia title in May with Jesus as Al-Nassr coach, and opened the scoring on Friday midway through the first half.

Kingsley Coman’s shot from outside the area was blocked by goalkeeper Waleed Abdullah, and Ronaldo was there to shoot home the rebound from close range for goal number 980 in his career.

Samu Costa added a second for Al-Nassr, coached by former Tottenham Hotspur boss Ange Postecoglou, just before the break, and Coman sealed the win with 13 minutes remaining.

Al-Qadsiah earlier thrashed Al-Kholood 5-0, with Dutch international Tijjani Reijnders opening the scoring and Italy’s Mateo Retegui and Mexico’s Julian Quinones also finding the target.

articles.summary: Vence por 3-2 a Francia en la final
articles.body: La selección española femenina de hockey línea se proclamó campeona del mundo tras ganar a Francia por 2-3 en la final de los World Skate Games de Asunción (Paraguay). España, en su cuarta final mundialista consecutiva, conquistó su segunda estrella. El combinado nacional había llegado a la final tras ganar todos sus partidos. Acabó la fase de grupos como primera. En la final se encontró de nuevo con Francia, a la que ya ganó en la primera fase gracias a un gol de oro en la prórroga. En esta ocasión, la selección española debió de tirar de remontada tras verse 2-0 abajo. Los tantos de Mercè Vilaró, al final del primer tiempo y de Alejandra Vallejo tras el descanso empataron el encuentro. En el último minuto, Olivia Monjas aprovechó una asistencia de Blanca López para marcar el tercer y definitivo tanto del encuentro. articles.title: West Indies beat India as Hope’s hundred secures record T20 chase
articles.summary: Shai Hope’s hundred and Sherfane Rutherford’s fifty lead West Indies in record 252 chase to level series 1-1.
articles.body:
Shai Hope has hit an unbeaten 102 off only 45 balls as the West Indies have beaten India in their highest successful Twenty20 run chase.

Hope hit nine sixes and six boundaries on Friday in his second T20 hundred as the West Indies finished with 252-4 in reply to India’s 249-5 and won by six wickets in Ranchi, India, with nine balls to spare.

Overall, it was the second highest successful run chase in T20 history. South Africa’s 259-4 was the highest against the West Indies in March.

Sherfane Rutherford played another supporting role to Hope with 84 off 37 balls, including seven sixes and seven fours.

For India, Sanju Samson scored 82 off 41 balls.

The five-match series stands at 1-1. Indore hosts the third T20 on Sunday.

The West Indies brought in left-arm spinner Gudakesh Motie and made India bat.

Samson and Abhishek Sharma scored 42 runs in 24 balls. Ishan Kishan hit a quick-fire 43 off 22 balls, and Samson reached 50 off 21 balls. Overall, he hit four sixes and nine fours.

India took 79-1 in the powerplay and brought up 100 off 8.1 overs. The Kishan-Samson partnership added 97 off only 43 balls.

Roston Chase then bowled Kishan in the 12th over and Shivam Dube two overs later. Chase finished with 3-24 in four overs.

India was down to 162-4 in the 15th over when Samson fell to Shamar Springer.

Shreyas Iyer hit 40 off 18 balls, accompanied by Tilak Varma’s 44 not out off 18 balls as the duo helped India finish on a high after hitting six sixes between them.

Despite their partnership of 83 from 32 balls, India fell shy of 250 but still achieved its eighth highest total in T20s.

Hope then led the West Indies’ charge by smoking 50 off 24 balls while losing three partners in the powerplay.

Mayank Yadav (3-36) bowled opener Kamil Pooran on four and Shimron Hetmyer for a golden duck.

Hope and Rovman Powell (24) resurrected the innings before Yadav got his third and bowled Powell.

That brought Hope and Rutherford together, and they added 120 off 54 balls.

Kuldeep Yadav sent back Rutherford in the 15th over, and the West Indies were still some distance away.

Romario Shepherd hit 34 off 13 balls with three sixes to provide the finishing flourish.

At the other end, Hope reached 100 off 45 balls, his second 50 coming off 21 balls.

It was Hope’s third century against India in four innings across T20s and ODIs .

images.caption: India captain Shreyas Iyer, right, looks on as West Indies captain Shai Hope, centre, celebrates his century and winning the second T20 international [Dibyangshu Sarkar/AFP]

articles.title: El padre del niño de 7 años que escaló El Capitán, denunciado a los Servicios de Protección Infantil
articles.standfirst: Joe Evermore desvela en una entrevista que se presentaron quejas contra él y su esposa una vez que su hijo Joey Danger ascendió esta mítica pared
articles.summary: Joe Evermore desvela en una entrevista que se presentaron quejas contra él y su esposa una vez que su hijo Joey Danger ascendió esta mítica pared
articles.body: Hace unos meses, Joey Danger Evermore se convirtió en la persona más joven en escalar El Capitán, la mítica 'pared' rocosa de Yosemite de 914 metros de altura. A sus 7 años y junto a su padre, completó la ascensión en cinco días y acompañado también por sus hermanos Sam y Sylvan y el equipo que documentaba audiovisualmente la ascensión Joey Danger cumplió los siete años mientras se encontraba en El Capitán. Sucedió a su hermano Sam en el ranking de los conquistadores más precoces de esta pared. Este había llegado a la cima en 2022 con ocho años (en 2025 también pisó la cima del Cervino, de 4.478 metros). Pronto surgieron las voces que cuestionaron la presencia de niños en El Capitán. Joe Evermore, padre de Joey, ha desvelado ahora en una entrevista con ABC7 que los Servicios de Protección Infantil recibieron varias quejas en las que se cuestionaban la forma en que él y su esposa educaban y cuidaban a sus hijos. "Algunas personas incluso han sugerido que nuestra paternidad merecía una investigación. Es difícil entender cómo alguien puede creer que Joey Danger estaría mejor separado de los padres que lo aman, entrenan a su lado, lo protegen, y lo están formando intencionalmente en un joven fuerte y capaz", escribió Joe en sus redes sociales. Las denuncias sostenían que los padres ponían en peligro a Joey al permitirle participar en una escalada de gran dificultad a una edad temprana. Evermore apuntó que las personas que habían obrado de este modo no tienen experiencia en escalada y que desconocen las condiciones y las medidas de seguridad que lleva aparejada esta actividad. "Admito que existen riesgos, pero creo que los beneficios superan con creces los riesgos. Como padre, estoy reduciendo esos riesgos con un equipo, con una buena preparación y con nuestra propia habilidad y nuestro propio entrenamiento", comenta Joe Evermore. Los Servicios de Protección Infantil decidieron no dar curso a las denuncias.

articles.title: El Galán más sincero: "Veo el número 1 muy cuesta arriba"
articles.standfirst: El madrileño no dudó en asegurar que sus opciones de alcanzar el trono del pádel se han complicado e intentarán mejorar el juego para mantener sus opciones.
articles.summary: El madrileño no dudó en asegurar que sus opciones de alcanzar el trono del pádel se han complicado e intentarán mejorar el juego para mantener sus opciones.
articles.body: Sincero, abierto y sin miedo, Ale Galán ha abordado la cuestión del número uno tras lograr la clasificación a semifinales en Düsseldorf y la crisis de resultados que atraviesan en los últimos meses. "En la Race, siendo muy honesto, lo veo complicado. Está muy cuesta arriba. Queda el final de temporada, pero es verdad que aquí el año pasado cambiaron las sensaciones y de repente empezamos a conseguir los resultados", se sinceraba Galán en rueda de prensa tras el pase a semifinales. Una respuesta directa a la cuestión más relevante de la realidad del pádel, que para Galán está marcada por algunos partidos que han dejado escapar a lo largo de la temporada y que les hacen tener una desventaja ya considerable en la carrera por el número uno de 1.780 puntos. "Este año los resultados no han acompañado cuando el juego estaba siendo altísimo y en algunos momentos se nos han escapado partidos siendo mejores que nuestros rivales. Y no solo Arturo y Agus, también algunos momentos de la temporada con algún que otro partido más", confesaba. Aún así el español prefiere evitar centrarse en las razones para focalizarse en el juego e intentar que, pase lo que pase, consigan dar las máximas alegrías a su entrenador en el año de la despedida. "Quiero centrarme en recuperar el mejor juego posible y los resultados, al final, serán el resultado. Nuestra intención con Jorge era darle todo, las máximas alegrías en este último año y eso es lo que vamos a intentar hacer, buscar nuestro mejor juego y ojalá así los puntos caigan de nuestro lado", finalizaba.

articles.title: F1 Singapore GP: Max Verstappen wins sprint, George Russell crashes out and McLarens collide
articles.summary: Russell took the lead at the start but threw it away at the end of lap one, and Verstappen prevailed
articles.body:
Max Verstappen took victory in the Singapore Grand Prix sprint race from pole position after George Russell crashed out of the lead at the end of the first lap.

A downpour soaked the starting grid 15 minutes before the scheduled start, while some parts of the Marina Bay Street Circuit remained dry. The race was delayed by half an hour due to the standing water in Turns 2 and 3.

When the sprint got underway, it was still a tale of two halves in terms of track conditions and all cars started on intermediate tyres after two formation laps.

Front-row starter Russell had a much better getaway than Verstappen and took the lead before Turn 1, with Lewis Hamilton up to third from sixth on the grid. Charles Leclerc, Oscar Piastri, Lando Norris, Kimi Antonelli, Liam Lawson and Pierre Gasly followed, with Isack Hadjar down to 11th.

Russell's lead was short-lived, as he lost control of his Silver Arrow on the kerb at the exit of the last corner and spun into the inside wall at the end of lap one. Meanwhile, Lance Stroll and Sergio Perez collided at Turn 16, with the Aston Martin coming to a halt against the barriers, and Isack Hadjar retired after reporting "the engine braking is dying".

The safety car was called into action, with the race neutralised for five laps – during which Arvid Lindblad spun, rejoining in last place after driving the wrong way down the track, and Franco Colapinto's race ended because of a technical issue.

Verstappen maintained the lead at the restart, while Oliver Bearman snatched eighth place away from Gasly after wheel-to-wheel action throughout sector one. The Alpine driver lost another two positions over the following two laps; he complained of being pushed wide by Nico Hulkenberg, but the stewards took no further action.

Verstappen's gap to Hamilton hovered between 0.7s and 1.4s from lap seven to lap 11 before the Red Bull racer significantly pulled away, with his advantage reaching three seconds at the end of lap 13 and five seconds by lap 16.

The intermediate compound was greatly suffering on the mostly dry track, so it was all about tyre management. Leclerc reported his front tyres were "destroyed"; the Ferrari driver was losing two seconds a lap to team-mate Hamilton and was caught by the McLarens and Antonelli with three laps remaining.

Norris dove down the inside of Piastri on the very last lap, but the papaya cars made contact and spun; the reigning world champion dropped down to eighth, while his Australian team-mate retired, costing the team eight points.

Meanwhile, Verstappen romped to victory with a reduced but healthy 2.6s-second lead over Hamilton, as Leclerc held off the papaya cars for third. Antonelli inherited fourth ahead of Lawson, Bearman and Hulkenberg.

articles.title: WWE's Roman Reigns Era is at a Crossroads
articles.summary: WWE wants fans to believe that Money in the Bank represents a serious possible turning point for Roman Reigns' title run as top dog and the prospects of LA Knight's status as a main-eventer.
articles.body:
WWE wants fans to believe that Money in the Bank represents a serious possible turning point for Roman Reigns' title run as top dog and the prospects of LA Knight's status as a main-eventer.

If WWE lets it stand as such, of course.

Should WWE do what many fans would consider to be the smart thing at this point, LA Knight will walk out as the winner in the main event.

Think about the fallout. Knight winning is yet another nod by WWE that getting over and performing at a high level for a long time will be rewarded. More so than a message to the locker room, it would be a message to the fanbase itself that, indeed, backing favorites will end up being a worthy time investment.

Don't forget the ramifications for Reigns. He'd be an infinitely more interesting character while going back in chase mode, too. He's great as a top guy, but some unexpected adversity before attempting to get the title back in time for WrestleMania (where he'll probably put over Oba Femi, too), would make for some compelling weekly programming.

Much of this has to do with Royce Keys' 946 faction. If they throw interference, the whole thing not only boosts Knight, it stamps a permanent exclamation mark on the hottest new thing in WWE. It doesn't get bigger than being the faction to stomp out the Bloodline and being the faction to suddenly halt another Reigns, well, reign of terror.

This doesn't have to be silly stable booking in an attempt to just set up Survivor Series, either. That event is at the end of November. Call this 946 vs. Bloodline beef a happy bonus. All of the above positive notes paint the justification more than anything else.

And no, the dusty finish via interference doesn't diminish Knight's accomplishment. That's like saying Sami Zayn hasn't had a worthwhile time since winning a title and only holding it for a few moments. He got the deserved career-long moment, cherished it with fans and remains in the mix, title or not.

Speaking of holding a title for just a few minutes, yes, there's always the specter of a cash-in attempt after the main event. Someone like a CM Punk or Penta with a briefcase could come cashing in and steal everything from Knight.

But what's the worst-case scenario? Knight's title win would still be official on his resume. The moment would still be earned and shared with fans. He got over the hump and isn't going anywhere as a main-eventer who can win it at any other point.

Call it a crossroads for Reigns, Knight and WWE, really. There are few better chances for Reigns to drop a title in a way that makes so much sense. There are few better spots for Knight to actually get a win, with WWE having plenty of ways, briefcase or otherwise, to get it back off him in a hurry, if so desired.

And now is the time for you deserve it runs. Guys like Cody Rhodes and Punk have dropped top titles in these efforts. Drew McIntyre and Zayn were the big winners here. Stretch it out a few years, and Damian Priest and Jey Uso, too.

No reason Knight can't join that list, especially now. What better way for WWE to keep sending the message to fans, too, that everything is worth watching?

The alternative to all this is Reigns just winning, probably with some of the faction drama for good measure. And to his credit, Reigns' current run has been fantastic, full-time and filled with elite defenses that didn't feature outside interference. It's perhaps as compelling as he's ever been.

Still, Reigns losing, Knight winning, briefcases and factions…it all becomes a lot more interesting on a weekly basis this way.

It's a crossroads, but really only if WWE has the confidence to veer off the expected path.

articles.title: BS Meter on Roman Reigns vs. LA Knight, Drew McIntyre Return Rumors, WrestleMania Location, More
articles.summary: WWE's Money in the Bank event continues to be a major staple of the pro wrestling calendar.
articles.body:
WWE's Money in the Bank event continues to be a major staple of the pro wrestling calendar.

Impressively, the pro wrestling rumor mill ramps up in a big way around the event, too, offering up some must-see buzz that doesn't even deal with which wrestlers might win the men's and women's briefcases.

Look at this week's lineup, which boasts things like injury fallout, WrestleMania rumblings, major return buzz and big future plans for the top stars in the company.

To help fans keep pace with the latest fast-paced rumor mill, let's throw the must-know rumors on the BS Meter, with 10 being the highest form of unbelievable buzz fans can safely dismiss.

Wondering how Rhea Ripley's injury changed other big plans? According to WrestleVotes (h/t Geno Mrosko of Cageside Seats), the injury actually led to the big character change for Damian Priest, too.

So, it's not just the women's title scene majorly impacted by the Ripley injury, it seems. Priest and R-Truth made sense as a fun team, but at the same time, they always sort of felt like they had an expiration date leading to this type of moment, too.

Again, it sort of feels like this was always the exit ramp for the tandem. But it also feels true that, were it not for the Ripley injury, stable/faction stuff would have kept them together for longer. Hence, this being one of the more 50-50 pieces of buzz this week.

About WrestleMania. According to Fightful Select (h/t Cain A. Knight of Cageside Seats), WWE and New Orleans have the rights to the Superdome in New Orleans in 2029 during the stretch of year that would include 'Mania.

Talk about a bill coming due. WWE had announced WrestleMania 42 would go to the Superdome in 2026, only to reverse course and send that event to Las Vegas. Speculation suggested WWE IOU'd a 'Mania for New Orleans, so 2029 might just be it.

There's fair speculation around the outlook for WrestleMania 43 in Saudi Arabia next year and speculation that WrestleMania 44 in 2028 will go to Nashville. Looping back to New Orleans after that would make plenty of sense.

Here's an eyebrow-raiser: According to Wrestling Observer Radio's Dave Meltzer (h/t Knight ), the finale for the feud between Bayley and Lyra Valkyria could be a "Hair Match."

Whoa, considering 2004 might be the last time WWE fans saw a women's hair match. WWE needs something as a feud-capper, though, considering Bayley lost to Valkyria in July, was off television until mid-September, then lost again.

Is this a serious plan or a thing that was thrown out to generate even more hype for an end-of-feud bout at a to-be-announced date? Impossible to say at this point, but odds are the stipulation was at least thrown on the list of possible ideas, right?

Is Big Cass getting a push or not? There might be a problem: According to Fightful Select (h/t Knight ), there are those in WWE worried that fan speculation about an Enzo Amore return is hurting Cass' creative booking.

This is really silly. It's on WWE creative, and to a lesser extent, on Cass, to find a way around this. If they throw out something more interesting than what's been on television so far, what the fans are speculating in the background won't matter as much.

Pretty unbelievable. This is the creative industry with the undead, demons and quite a bit more. There are ways around this supposed issue. And really, it feels like Cass was brought back to put over other talent, not go title-hunting himself. And yes, everyone is wondering when the Amore return happens, but that isn't holding anyone back.

Drew McIntyre could be back soon, it seems. According to WrestleVotes Radio (h/t Knight ), McIntyre's return could see him come back on the Raw show instead of SmackDown, with the blue brand already boasting such a top-heavy scene.

More star power for Raw is never a bad thing and, really, there's three fun factions for McIntyre to bounce off of on the red brand right now. Even if it's just sparring with The Vision or something, he adds some serious credibility to the whole thing.

This is more of a when and not an if situation. SmackDown just has far too much going on at the very top right now. McIntyre, out since WrestleMania 42 in April, is one of those guys who can afford to wait on the proper creative.

Roman Reigns might not lose a title to LA Knight over the weekend, but the feud might mean he undergoes some changes. According to WrestleVotes Radio (h/t Knight ), a recent promo battle that featured Reigns more emotional than usual has WWE creative looking to harness that more.

The promo battle from Raw was certainly a fun one. And Reigns displayed a pretty unexpected amount of character shift while verbally sparring with Knight, too. If that was a preview of what's to come, it's going to be super fun to watch Reigns on a weekly basis.

Who knew Reigns could keep evolving? He's already silencing critics with a full-time run that doesn't rely on interference to retain. He's top dog for a reason. And yet, indeed, one promo sure felt like a glimpse of what's to come from him, regardless of whether he has gold around his waist.

articles.title: Hornets Must Limit Turnovers To Beat Bucks In Sunday Game
articles.summary: Charlotte's 25 turnovers cost them against Brooklyn. Per Yahoo Sports, the Hornets must fix ball security to survive Sunday's matchup with Milwaukee.
articles.body:
Tuesday night saw the Charlotte Hornets suffer a severe blow. They fell to the Brooklyn Nets 124-90 at Spectrum Center. It was a bad loss, but the real story is the ball security. The team coughed up the rock 25 times. That is too many. If the Hornets want to beat the Milwaukee Bucks on Sunday, October 11, they have to stop giving the ball away. It is that simple. You cannot win with careless play.

Fix the Turnovers or Get Blown Out Again

Charlotte was missing key players like Coby White and Brandon Miller. Yet the lack of control was still the main problem. Per Yahoo Sports , the Hornets were just too careless with the basketball. They had 25 team turnovers against the Nets. Dennis Schroder is the only true point guard who is healthy right now. The rest of the group is just secondary playmakers trying to make things happen. This creates chaos. The Bucks will punish every mistake. The coaching staff needs to tighten up the offense before Sunday.

Fans are excited to see the new draft pick, Hannes Steinbach. He was the 14th overall pick. But his start was slow. Steinbach remained on the bench until the third quarter was nearly over. He finished with 7 points and 4 rebounds in 14 minutes. Yahoo Sports notes that lottery picks rarely join preseason action that late. The Hornets have a very deep frontcourt. This makes minutes hard to come by. If Steinbach sits out again against Milwaukee, fans should question his spot in the rotation. Head Coach Charles Lee has to figure out how to use him better. The rookie showed some promise, but he needs more time on the floor to prove he belongs.

The roster is changing fast. Michael Ajayi has arrived from Butler. He played 19 minutes and had 3 points and 4 rebounds. His defense is his best trait. He is destined to be a two-way guy this year. He will split time with the Greensboro Swarm. But there is bigger news off the court. Analyst Zach Buckley wrote that the Hornets should trade Grant Williams this season. Williams makes $14,265,750 this season. That is a lot of money for a backup. Per Yahoo Sports, trading him could give Tidjane Salaün more playing time. The 21-year-old French forward shot 50.3% from the field last season.

articles.body:
Tottenham Injury Update Ahead of Manchester United Clash

Tottenham head to Old Trafford with a mixed injury picture, but there is at least some good news for Roberto De Zerbi before the meeting with Manchester United. Micky van de Ven and Jan Paul van Hecke are both expected to be available, which matters given how stretched Spurs have looked at the back.

Both defenders picked up issues while away with the Netherlands, Van Hecke with a foot problem, Van de Ven with a hand injury. Neither now appears serious enough to rule them out. De Zerbi did, however, admit there is an "emotional aspect" around Van Hecke after his wife gave birth to twins this week. That does not mean he misses out, it means the manager has one more thing to weigh up before naming his side.

For Tottenham, getting Van de Ven and Van Hecke back is straightforwardly important. Pedro Porro remains unavailable after the hamstring injury suffered in the 3-2 defeat to Aston Villa, and he is still not ready despite seeing a specialist in Spain during the international break. That leaves Spurs without one of their more reliable wide options and keeps pressure on the rest of the defensive unit.

Dejan Kulusevski is closer, but not back. After more than 500 days out with a complicated patella injury and two separate surgeries, he has returned to training and featured in an internal 11-a-side game. There was a minor setback, which explains the caution. De Zerbi confirmed he will travel with the squad in a support role for now, much like James Maddison did before returning late last season from an anterior cruciate ligament injury.

Maddison is available, though De Zerbi conceded the midfielder had a minor setback and was unable to train pain-free earlier this week. Mykhailo Mudryk is still a few weeks away with ankle ligament damage, while Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert remain out long term.

Predicted Tottenham XI: Kinsky, Gray, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Udogie, Bentancur, Tonali, Gallagher, Savio, Marmoush, Tel.

For Spurs, this is not about perfection. It is about having enough senior bodies back for a difficult away game.

articles.title: The Titans’ Offensive Line Faces Its Biggest Test Against Houston’s Pass Rush
articles.summary: The winless Tennessee Titans return home this weekend to face the just-as-winless Houston Texans in a divisional matchup as they try to climb out of the cell...
articles.body:
The winless Tennessee Titans return home this weekend to face the just-as-winless Houston Texans in a divisional clash as they try to climb out of the cellar. One key matchup to look out for is the Titans offensive line against the Texans' defensive front. Houston has racked up 14 sacks so far this year , good for third-best in the NFL.

The Titans offensive line, much-maligned going into the season, has actually only allowed six total sacks through four games, tied for 5th fewest in the league. A closer look shows that they allow 10.3 pressures per game , 8th most in the league.

If the Titans are going to get their first win, the banged-up offensive line will need to give quarterback Cam Ward time to throw against a talented defensive line. How do the Titans match up against the Texans' defensive front?

The Titans' Offensive Line Faces Its Biggest Test Against Houston's Pass Rush

Two-time Pro Bowler Will Anderson is off to another strong start for the Texans in 2026. He's registered 4.5 sacks and 11 quarterback hits in his first four games. His ability to generate pressure even when double-teamed makes him dangerous on just about any passing play. One good piece of news for Titans fans is that the team managed to keep Anderson under relative control in 2025 , allowing him to only get one sack and two QB hits in the two matchups.

Another reason for Tennessee to have some hope of stopping Anderson has been the play of left tackle JC Latham so far this year. Through four games, he has allowed zero sacks or QB hits, and four total pressures . Latham's strong start has been one of the bright spots for a Titans offensive line that entered the season with plenty of questions.

However, Tennessee may still need to provide Latham with additional help on passing downs. Chips from tight ends or running backs could slow Anderson's rush, although keeping extra blockers in protection would leave Ward with fewer options downfield. The Titans must find the right balance between protecting their quarterback and allowing their passing game to operate.

Ultimately, the goal is not necessarily to eliminate Anderson from the game. Tennessee needs to prevent him from consistently disrupting Ward's timing and forcing him into difficult situations. Against a pass rusher of Anderson's caliber, even a handful of critical pressures could determine whether the Titans' offense finds a rhythm.

Houston's Interior Rush Could Be Just as Important

The Texans' pass rush presents more than a challenge on the edges. Tennessee must also account for pressure up the middle, where its interior offensive linemen will be responsible for keeping Ward's pocket from collapsing.

Defensive tackle Tommy Togiai has generated nine QB pressures to start the year, though he's still looking for his first sack. Next to him is veteran Sheldon Rankins , who has notched two sacks along with 14 QB pressures. Dealing with these two beasts on the interior of the offensive line will be the responsibility of center Austin Schlottmann and guards Peter Skoronski and Atonio Mafi.

Skoronski and Schlottmann have yet to allow a sack this year, and it'll take another Herculean effort to keep it that way. Mafi has only allowed one sack, but it's been a limited sample as he's filled in for promising rookie Fernando Carmona Jr., who is sidelined with a severe ankle sprain.

With Rankins and Togiai capable of generating pressure from the interior, communication between the guards and center will be critical. If Houston can push the pocket backward, Ward could be forced off his spot even when the Titans' tackles successfully contain Anderson and the other edge rushers.

The Titans' improved offensive line will face its toughest test this weekend in Nashville. All of the matchups and schemes have to come together to keep the heat off Ward. As Ward has slowly improved game over game this year, the offensive line play has been a big factor in that. Falling victim to the heat of Anderson and friends would not only be troublesome for the Titans in trying to get their first win, but it could also put a halt to the confidence-building of Ward.

Bonus Pick(!): Off the schneid last week with the backdoor cover, bringing the season record to 1-3. The Texans are giving 7.5 points on the road here, even after their rough 0-4 start. None of the Titans' games this year have been pretty so far, but they've managed to hang around ever since the opener. Titans +7.5 is the play.

articles.title: Brutal Hit By Blackhawk Frank Nazar Stuns Islanders On Horvat
articles.summary: Bo Horvat's status is unclear after a hit on Frank Nazar. Get the latest on the suspension and what it means for the Islanders' lineup.
articles.body:
The New York Islanders are waiting to see if captain Bo Horvat can play Saturday against the Tampa Bay Lightning. The team pulled him from Thursday's game right after he took a hard hit to the head. Frank Nazar of the Chicago Blackhawks delivered the illegal check that knocked Horvat out. The league's concussion spotters saw the hit and sent Horvat to the locker room immediately.

Coach Pete DeBoer said the team is still figuring out the next steps. "I think he's going to see our people again this morning and see how he feels," DeBoer said. The team did not have a full practice on Friday. Horvat sat out of the optional session at UBS Arena. His status for the weekend game remains uncertain as the medical staff checks on him.

Things got heated late in the third period of Thursday's match. The Islanders led 3-1 with 1:33 left on the clock. Horvat shot the puck into the empty net for his second goal of the game. He was upended by a shoulder to the head area right after the shot. Nazar received a five-minute match misconduct for the illegal check to the head. Following a Friday hearing, the league suspended Nazar for two games. This penalty removes him from the lineup for two upcoming Blackhawks contests.

Players on both sides had strong words about the play. Emil Heineman called it a cheap shot. "It's a cheap shot I would say. I don't like to see that and I like the way we responded," Heineman said. He noted that the team has to stick up for its own. "They go after one of our guys…whatever it is we have to stick up for one of ours and I think we did that," he added. Per Audacy , Logan Stanley also spoke up to support his captain.

The Islanders feel the loss of their top scorer. Horvat leads the team with four goals in just four games. He also led the squad with 31 goals last season. He was the only Islander named to an Olympic team. Losing him hurts the offense. Kyle Palmieri thinks the hit was too rough. "I definitely think [the hit] was over the line," Palmieri said. He also noted that the game moves fast and players must protect themselves.

Coach DeBoer agreed that the call was correct. "I think they got the call right. We'll see, but you don't like to see that on anybody," DeBoer said. The team is in the early stages of getting their leader back. "We're still in the initial phase of return to play," DeBoer noted. The staff is not ready to discuss long-term plans yet. "We're not even having those conversations yet," he stated.

Islanders fans need to watch the news closely before Saturday night. The team needs Horvat to keep their early-season pace going. He was the only player to score twice in the win against Chicago. While the team responded well to the hit, the injury to their captain is the main story. The Blackhawks lose a key player too, but the Islanders face a bigger immediate risk.

Logan Stanley showed his support for the group. "That's our captain…that's our leader. It doesn't matter who it is. You come after one of us…you gotta come after all of us," Stanley said. He credited the team for sticking up for Horvat. The team will need that same unity if Horvat cannot play. The Lightning present a tough test if the Islanders are without their top center. The next 24 hours will decide the lineup for the weekend.

articles.title: On the Yankees’ playoff failures and the agony of apathy
articles.summary: What to do when it doesn’t hurt anymore
articles.body:
I try very hard to fight back against apathy. In politics, the economy, media, the world begs for your apathy. Don't make a fuss, let it all just happen. It's all going According to Plan. The state apparatus depends on your apathy. Do not give them that gift.

And yet, not quite 48 hours after the Yankees once again lost in the ALDS, lost to a team seeded higher than them, lost to a team that is just so fundamentally annoying that thinking about them raises my blood pressure a point or two…I don't feel much at all.

I've always tried to hedge my reactions to bad sports news. The Don LeGreca-style rants make for good radio and some of the longer, more unhinged comments we get here are fun to scroll past, but at the end of the day I consume baseball for my own entertainment. Letting yourself get mad over something you say you enjoy while having 0 control over it hasn't made a whole lot of sense to me. Let sports lift you up, not press you down.

And true to form, I'm not mad about the 2026 Yankees. I'm beige. The Yankees dogwalked the Red Sox last week only to find themselves canine-ized by the Rays, swept out of the ALDS in what's actually a worse result than last year. (They lasted a whole four games against the Blue Jays!) Aaron Boone put the worst leadoff hitter in baseball atop the lineup, telling us that he liked the potential for action on the basepaths ahead of the only batter who showed up in the series, and that leadoff hitter went 0-for-5 as the team died—with him as the final out—because of course he did.

I don't quite know why I'm so numb to all of this. The Yankees won 93 games, the second-best record in the AL, without the game's best player, while actively rehabbing three pitchers in their starting rotation, while Austin Wells was locked in the trunk of a car for four months, while shortstop was an open question until the season's final few weeks. It should be kind of remarkable that they were even in the dance in the first place?

But the AL was so bad, the table so uncompetitive, that the Yankees didn't really outrun the other guy being chased by the bear. There was no bear at all. The team wasn't good enough to chase down the Rays, dooming themselves to an additional two playoff games while the Rays got to rest, prepare, and welcome the Yankees to the Trop for the start of the series. The same offense we'd seen sleepwalk through the year for weeks at a time showed themselves, they lost, and I don't really care.

Supposedly at the staff level the organization is starting to pick at itself like an under-stimulated pet bird. This annual tradition of "just be good enough to make it before 26 people who should be among the best in the world at what they do collectively forget what their jobs are" might finally be sinking in. At the top level though we'll be told not to worry, There is A Plan, these guys are having good at bats actually, it's right in front of us.

Congratulations to the New York Yankees. You've managed to accomplish something my government and AI companies haven't. Sure, man, whatever you say, I shrug my shoulders and I walk down the street.

articles.title: Justin Jefferson, Ja’Marr Chase and more WR injury updates for Week 5
articles.summary: The two LSU alums headline the wide receivers we're monitoring ahead of Sunday's action.
articles.body:
With Sunday almost here, we're doing our latest wide receiver injury round-up, which features the likes of Justin Jefferson and Ja'Marr Chase , along with several others.

Before we get to those with designations, some of the wide receivers who have been removed from injury reports include Malik Nabers, Chris Olave, Dontayvion Wicks and Mike Evans, all of whom are good to go.

On the other end of the spectrum, players such as DeVonta Smith, Stefon Diggs and Quentin Johnston have already been ruled out for Week 5.

Now, here's what we know about players who have been given the questionable tag ahead of Sunday.

Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson (18) looks on during warmups prior to the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium. Credit: Kim Klement Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

After not practicing at all last week before being ruled out with his ankle injury, Jefferson saw an uptick in participation this week with three limited practices, which earned him a questionable tag .

The progress Jefferson made in practice suggests he's close, and he sounded optimistic when speaking to the media.

"It feels good now. Hopefully, Sunday, being able to rock and roll," Jefferson said, per Will Ragatz of Bring Me The News .

It seems like he's got a better chance to play than not, but the Vikings also have a bye in Week 6 and a 4-0 record, so it wouldn't be shocking to see Minnesota hold Jefferson out for another week.

Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'marr Chase (1) walks for the locker room after the fourth quarter of the NFL Week 1 game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Chase saw back-to-back days of upgraded practice participation as he works through the concussion protocol.

He didn't practice on Wednesday before being limited on Thursday and full on Friday, but he still has the questionable tag.

The last step is getting cleared by an independent neurologist, which appears likely to happen on Saturday given his full practice to close out the week.

Nothing is confirmed yet, but we expect Chase to play.

Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers (4) celebrates after he scores a touchdown against the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium. Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

After battling a hamstring injury for multiple weeks, it's now a foot issue for Zay Flowers, who was limited three times this week before being deemed questionable.

But ESPN's Jamison Hensley said that, despite the questionable tag, Flowers is "expected to play" in Week 5.

If Flowers isn't upgraded and removed from the injury report on Saturday, we'll be on the lookout for reports about his status on Sunday morning and afternoon.

Otherwise, we won't know for sure whether or not Flowers is playing until an hour and a half before the 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff on Sunday night.

Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb (88) reacts after a fourth quarter touchdown against the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium. Credit: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

CeeDee Lamb exited the Dallas Cowboys' embarrassing Week 5 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers with a quadriceps injury .

Thankfully, it doesn't appear he has anything significant, as it's just a bruise, and the expectation is he'll be good to go in Week 6 after Dallas' mini bye.

"My understanding is that it is a quad bruise," NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported. "Do not expect this to be a long-term injury."

Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins (5) throws a ball to a young fan during pregame before the first quarter of the NFL Preseason game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Detroit Lions at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Like his teammate Chase, Tee Higgins closed out the week with a full practice after not taking part on Wednesday and Thursday because of groin and neck issues.

Head coach Zac Taylor wouldn't commit to Higgins playing in spite of the questionable tag , but the full practice on Friday suggests he has a good chance to do so.

We expect Higgins will be active in Week 5.

Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Ladd McConkey (15) looks on during warm ups prior to the game against the Buffalo Bills at New Highmark Stadium. Credit: Mark Konezny-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Ladd McConkey didn't practice at all this week because of a foot injury and was then given a questionable tag.

The lack of participation amounted to a downgrade from last week, when the Chargers wide receiver was at least able to practice on a limited basis twice with the same issue before suiting up.

With the downgrade, we suspect McConkey is more likely to sit than play.

Washington Commanders wide receiver Terry McLaurin (17) reacts after making a touchdown catch against the Seattle Seahawks in the second half at Northwest Stadium. Credit: Amber Searls-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Terry McLaurin is once again questionable to play this week with the hamstring injury that kept him sidelined in Week 4.

The veteran wide receiver didn't practice over the first two days of the week before turning in a limited session on Friday.

The uptick in practice participation gives him a chance to play, and head coach Dan Quinn said McLaurin is going in the right direction.

Even still, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reports that McLaurin will "most likely" be a game-time decision on Sunday.

Based on Quinn's comment, we'd give McLaurin a better than 50/50 chance to play.

Buffalo Bills wide receiver DJ Moore (2) celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Houston Texans during the first half at Reliant Stadium. Credit: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

DJ Moore has sat out each of the first two practices of the week because of his shoulder injury that he reaggravated last week, forcing his early exit.

Moore doesn't need to practice to play, but we sure would like to see at least some limited work on Saturday. Either way, he's likely headed for a questionable tag.

Because he has already reaggravated the injury, the Bills might think it wise to hold him out a week, even if he's capable of playing at less than 100%.

We'll know more on Saturday, when the Bills drop their final injury report.

Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jordan Addison (3) celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Chicago Bears at U.S. Bank Stadium. Credit: Jeffrey Becker-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

A new addition to the injury report this week, Jordan Addison is questionable to play with his hamstring injury.

He turned in two limited practices after sitting out on Wednesday, so he's trending in a positive direction ahead of Sunday.

As is the case with Jefferson, don't be surprised if the 4-0 record and the upcoming bye week factor into the Vikings' decision. For now, we'd put Addison at about a 50/50 chance to play.

Tennessee Titans wider receiver Carnell Tate (14) runs with the ball after a made catch during day 1 of mini-camp at Vanderbilt Health Football Center. Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Carnell Tate finally had a big game in Week 4, but the concern here is that the rookie was a midweek addition to the injury report with a back issue.

The Titans wideout was limited on Thursday and Friday before drawing the questionable tag.

However, head coach Robert Saleh told reporters Tate is just dealing with some tightness and should be good to go .
